title: Chart & DOM trading interactions
body:
## Context
R3 closes the execution loop. E29 gives the OMS and its state machine, E30 gives the order ticket, E21 gives the readable DOM ladder, E32 gives brackets and the native-SL invariant. **E31 is the direct-manipulation layer on top of all of them**: trading *where you analyse* — on the chart price axis and on the DOM ladder rows — instead of retyping into a ticket.

Per `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 the epic delivers: draggable order and position lines with drag-to-amend and snap-to-tick, drag SL/TP from the position tool, click-to-trade on the ladder, one-click flatten and reverse with a configurable confirmation policy, overlays that never degrade under the frame-budget shedding ladder, and an undo window for accidental drags.

Every path added here is an order-placing path, so it inherits the R3 safety rules verbatim: arm/lock gating (US-ORD-005 / CMP-229), the native exchange-side stop-loss invariant (US-ORD-013, enforced server-side by E32/M17 — **this epic never bypasses it**), risk caps and kill-switch (E39), and full auditing of every click/drag with the price row and modifier used.

## Scope
**User stories (all of the chart/DOM direct-manipulation half of domain ORD, plus the two DOM trading stories):**
- US-ORD-007 Order from chart (Must)
- US-ORD-008 Drag order, stop and target lines (Must)
- US-ORD-009 Cancel order from chart and DOM (Should)
- US-ORD-010 Flatten and cancel-all (Must)
- US-ORD-011 Reverse position (Should)
- US-DOM-007 Click-to-trade from the DOM (Should)
- US-DOM-008 Drag to modify from the DOM (Should)

**Screens:** SCR-030 (chart panel trading layer), SCR-040 (chart trading overlay settings), SCR-050 (ladder trading affordances), SCR-063 (flatten entry points), SCR-064 (position SL/TP editor as the keyboard alternative), SCR-072 (flatten/cancel-all confirmation), SCR-076 (order confirmation modal), SCR-077 (rejection drawer reuse).

**Components:** CMP-192 OrderLineOverlay, CMP-229 ArmToggle, CMP-230 OwnOrderMarker, CMP-119 BracketEditor, CMP-120 TrailingStopEditor, CMP-130 SlippageEstimateChip, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-232 LimitsChip, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge.

**Backend/API consumed (not created here):** `POST /api/v1/orders`, `PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `DELETE /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `POST /api/v1/orders/cancel-all`, `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/close`, `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/reverse`, `PUT /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/tpsl`, `POST /api/v1/positions/close-all`, `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`; WS `orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`. Module **M14** (OMS) gains a thin *chart-trading intent* facade and audit-event enrichment only.

## Out of scope
- The order ticket form itself, sizing rules, hotkey infrastructure (E30).
- OMS state machine, reconciliation, blotters (E29).
- Bracket objects, scaled ladders, native-SL enforcement logic (E32).
- Emulated algos (E33), fan-out governor (E34), rule engine (E35–E37).
- DOM ladder rendering, heatmap, depth tiers (E21) — this epic only adds the trading affordances on top.
- Android; separate admin app; non-Bybit venues; non-USDT-perp instruments.

## Exit criteria
1. Every one of the seven user stories has its Gherkin scenarios passing in CI (unit + E2E), including the failure scenarios (amend rejected, drop on wrong side, already-filled cancel, nothing to flatten, insufficient margin on reverse).
2. **Safety:** an automated suite proves no chart drag, chart click, DOM click or DOM drag can open a position without a native exchange-side SL, and none is operable while disarmed, locked-out or kill-switched. Zero escapes (R3 exit criterion 2).
3. **Latency:** chart/DOM click → submit ≤50 ms client-side p95; click → ack p95 <300 ms on demo (budget #4); amend round trip ≤500 ms p95.
4. **Frame budget:** with 20 order/position lines plus a live ladder, the trading overlay layer redraws in ≤2 ms and order-line/position updates are *never* shed (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3 "never acceptable" list) — proven by a benchmark under the stress scenario.
5. **A11y:** every drag has a verified keyboard equivalent (focus line → arrow keys by tick → Enter to commit; ladder row → Enter → row action menu), announced pending/confirmed/rejected states, ≥24 px targets, no colour-only side encoding.
6. Undo window works: an accidental drag or click-trade can be reverted inside the configured window, with the revert itself audited.
7. Design QA, a11y audit, QA sign-off and Security sign-off all recorded; coverage ≥85 % on touched backend/engine packages, ≥80 % frontend.

## Risks
- **R2 Render performance** — trading overlays share the chart frame with footprint + heatmap; mitigated by a dedicated overlay layer with its own budget and by the "never shed trading data" rule.
- **R11 Alert reliability / mis-execution** — optimistic UI showing an amend that never landed; mitigated by pending states reconciled against exchange truth within 1 s and by spring-back on reject.
- **R5 Scope** — drag semantics can grow without bound; the undo window and modifier map are frozen by design sign-off before build.
- Fat-finger risk is the headline abuse case: covered by arm gating, confirm policy, notional thresholds and the undo window (E31-X02).

## Dependency graph
```
E11 chart engine (R1)          ─┐
E21 DOM ladder (R2)            ─┼─> E31-K01 spike (S16, render/input only, submits nothing)
E29 OMS + private WS (ends S16)─┼─> E31-T01 intent layer (S17) ─> E31-S01, E31-S04 (S17)
E39 risk caps/kill-switch(S16) ─┘
E30 order ticket (ends S17)    ─┬─> E31-S02, S03, S05, S06 (S18, strictly after)
E32 native-SL invariant (S17)  ─┘
```

**Sequencing rule applied throughout this epic: no E31 ticket is scheduled in the same sprint in which one of its blockers completes.**

| E31 tickets | Sprint | Heaviest blocker | Blocker completes | Slack |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D01 | 14 | E21 | R2 | design-ahead, 3 sprints |
| D02, D03 | 15 | E31-D01 | end S14 | design-ahead, 2 sprints |
| K01 | 16 | E11, E21 | R1 / R2 | ≥1 train |
| T01, S01, S04, Q01, X01 | 17 | E29, E39 | end S16 | starts the following sprint |
| S02, S03, S05, S06, D07, Q02, X02, T02 | 18 | E30, E32 | end S17 | starts the following sprint |

The S17 cohort deliberately carries **only** work whose blockers closed in S16; everything needing E30's arm/lock and confirmation policy or E32's native-SL invariant is deferred to S18. **E31-K01 is pulled forward to S16** (a render/input experiment on recorded data — no OMS, no API keys, submits nothing) so the latency and hit-testing unknowns are closed before the train opens; that pull-forward is the epic's schedule slack. **E31-X01 moved from S16 to S17** for the same reason — it previously ran concurrently with E29's and E39's completion sprint instead of after it.

**Design track (design-ahead, `00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence).** E31-D01 Done end of **S14**; E31-D02 — which carries *all* design-system contributions, the motion spec and the a11y design review — Done end of **S15**; E31-D03 handoff Done end of **S15**. That is two to three sprints ahead of the first consuming FE story (S17). **E31-D07 is a post-build design-QA audit only**, contributes no design-system entries, and therefore does not violate the design-ahead rule by sitting in S18.

## Story list
Children sum to **26 points**, mirroring `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2.

| Key | Kind | Title | Pts | Sprint |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E31-D01 | Task | UX research and hi-fi design for the chart trading layer (SCR-030, SCR-040) | 2 | 14 |
| E31-D02 | Task | Hi-fi DOM trading, design-system, motion spec and a11y review | 2 | 15 |
| E31-D03 | Task | Design handoff package for chart and DOM trading | 1 | 15 |
| E31-K01 | Spike | Prove drag latency, overlay hit-testing and the trading-layer frame budget | 1 | 16 |
| E31-T01 | Task | Chart/DOM trading intent layer: guards, optimistic state, undo window and audit | 2 | 17 |
| E31-S01 | Story | Place an order by clicking a price on the chart | 2 | 17 |
| E31-S04 | Story | Click-to-trade on the DOM ladder | 2 | 17 |
| E31-Q01 | Task | Test plan and E2E suite for chart and DOM trading | 1 | 17 |
| E31-X01 | Task | STRIDE threat model for chart and DOM trading interactions | 1 | 17 |
| E31-S02 | Story | Drag order, stop and target lines on the chart to amend | 3 | 18 |
| E31-S03 | Story | Cancel orders from the chart and the DOM ladder | 1 | 18 |
| E31-S05 | Story | Drag an order marker on the ladder to reprice it | 1 | 18 |
| E31-S06 | Story | One-click flatten, cancel-all and reverse with the confirmation policy | 2 | 18 |
| E31-D07 | Task | Design QA of shipped chart and DOM trading | 1 | 18 |
| E31-Q02 | Task | Perf, chaos and a11y audit plus QA sign-off | 2 | 18 |
| E31-X02 | Task | Abuse cases, RBAC/arm bypass checks and security sign-off | 1 | 18 |
| E31-T02 | Chore | Reconcile plan docs with the shipped chart and DOM trading behaviour | 1 | 18 |
| **Total** | | | **26** | |

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The whole direct-manipulation loop works on demo
  Given an armed chart and ladder on BTCUSDT with a demo account selected
  When I Shift+click a price to place a limit, drag its line to reprice, drag the SL, then flatten
  Then each action is acknowledged by the exchange, mirrored by the WS orders/positions topics,
  audited with the modifier and price used, and the position never exists without a native stop

Scenario: Nothing is operable when it must not be
  Given one-click is disarmed, or the kill-switch is engaged, or a risk lockout is active
  Then no chart click, chart drag, ladder click or ladder drag can submit anything,
  and each attempt shows the reason and is logged

Scenario: Overlays hold under load
  Given 100k bars, footprint on, a 200-depth heatmap and 20 working order lines
  Then the shedding ladder degrades heatmap cadence and footprint text first,
  order and position lines keep updating every frame, and fps stays above 30
```

## Technical notes / design
The frontend never talks to Bybit. All actions go through the existing REST endpoints and are confirmed by the private WS topics, which remain the source of truth (ADR-0006). Optimistic UI is allowed only as a *pending* visual state that must reconcile within 1 s or spring back.

**Sizing note.** `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 fixes E31 at **26 points**; the epic ticket estimate mirrors that rollup exactly and every child is sized against it (children sum to 26). The earlier draft sized this epic at 82 points by splitting the design, QA and security tracks into one ticket per activity; those tracks have been consolidated (D01+D02, D03+D04+D05, Q01+Q02, Q03+Q04+Q05+Q06, X02+X03) with no loss of scope — every deliverable, acceptance criterion and sign-off from the merged tickets is preserved in the surviving ticket bodies. Work that would push the epic past its 26-point budget is merged into a sibling or explicitly deferred, never silently re-sized.

## Test plan
Rolls up the child test plans; epic-level gates are the R3 §7.4 rows for Safety (native-SL suite as a required check), E2E (chart trading, DOM trading), A11y (ladder keyboard-operable) and Design (D-tickets Done ≥2 sprints ahead).

## Security notes
All child tickets touch `area/oms-execution` order placement, therefore are `security`-labelled for DoD purposes per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 whether or not the label was applied at creation.

## Accessibility notes
No drag-only affordance may ship. SCR-064 is the declared keyboard alternative for SL/TP manipulation; CMP-192 lines are DOM-mirrored and focusable; ladder rows are a roving-tabindex grid.

## Performance notes
Budget #4 (order ack) and §4.3 (shedding ladder) are the gates; the trading overlay layer has a ≤2 ms redraw budget per SCR-040.

## Observability
`order.submitted`, `order.amend_requested`, `order.cancel_requested`, `position.flattened`, `position.reversed`, `trading.chart_drag_modify_enabled` audit events; analytics `chart.trade_from_chart`, `dom.click_trade`, `trading.undo_used`; metrics `cv_chart_trade_click_to_submit_ms`, `cv_trading_overlay_redraw_ms`, `cv_trading_undo_total`.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 — 100 % child rollup, epic-level AC verified end-to-end on demo, coverage floors, docs updated, a11y verified, perf recorded, STRIDE finalised and signed off, QA epic-level regression pass, demoed to the Owner, retro note.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E29** (OMS + private WS mirror, ends S16), **E39** (risk caps, lockouts, kill-switch, ends S16), **E11** (chart engine interaction/hit-testing, R1), **E21** (ladder surface, R2), **E30** (ticket, arm/lock, hotkeys, confirm policy, ends S17) and **E32** (native-SL invariant + brackets, ends S17).

E11/E21/E29/E39 gate the Sprint-17 cohort; E30/E32 gate the Sprint-18 cohort. See the Dependency graph section for the per-ticket sprint-vs-blocker slack table.

## Branch
`feat/e31-chart-dom-trading` (epic umbrella; children branch as `feat/e31-<short>`). PRs ≤400 LOC.

title: UX research and hi-fi design for the chart trading layer (SCR-030, SCR-040)
body:
## Context
E31 introduces direct-manipulation trading (US-ORD-007..011, US-DOM-007..008) — the highest-consequence interaction in the product: a stray mouse-down can open real risk. Before any pixels are drawn we must settle the interaction vocabulary (which modifier does what, what is draggable, what confirms, what can be undone) against how the Owner and the account managers actually work today in TradingView/DeepCharts-class tools.

This is net-new interaction, so `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 design-ready and the planning brief's design-ahead rule (≥2 sprints) require research first, landing in Sprint 13 so hi-fi can be Done by Sprint 15 for build in Sprint 17.

SCR-030 is the spine of the product and already carries footprint cells, drawings, indicators and profile overlays. E31 adds the **trading layer**: position line (avg price, size, uPnL, R), SL/TP lines, working-order lines, fill markers, fan-out sibling ghost lines, liquidation-estimate line, break-even line and the arm-state display. SCR-040 is the modal that toggles each of those elements and the drag-to-modify behaviour.

Design must be Done by end of Sprint 15 so the FE stories (E31-S01/S02, Sprint 17) satisfy the design-ahead rule.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Research plan + 3–5 moderated sessions with the Owner and account-manager personas (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`) using the existing SCR-030 chart and SCR-050 ladder builds from R1/R2 as a think-aloud prop.
- Answer, with evidence, for SCR-030 / SCR-050:
  - Which modifier map is expected for chart order entry (the catalogue currently states `Ctrl+drag` on the price axis = limit, `Alt+click` = market at market; US-ORD-007 states `Shift+click` = limit on the opposite side, `Ctrl+click` = reduce-only stop — **this conflict must be resolved and the winner written back into `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030 and `11-user-stories.md` US-ORD-007**).
  - Whether drag-to-amend should commit on release or require a release-then-confirm for live.
  - Acceptable undo window length and its affordance (toast with Undo vs. Ctrl+Z) for accidental drags/clicks.
  - Expectation for ladder left-click vs right-click vs Ctrl+click (US-DOM-007 says left = limit at row, Ctrl = market, Escape = cancel-all).
  - Confirmation tolerance: where does confirmation feel protective vs. obstructive (feeds the configurable confirm policy owned by E30/SCR-076).
- A written **interaction vocabulary decision record** (modifier map table) appended to the SCR-040 entry, signed by the Owner.
- Findings note in `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md` F6/F7 annotations.

- Hi-fi Figma frames for **SCR-030 trading layer** covering every element listed in the SCR-040 catalogue entry: position line, SL line, TP line, working-order lines (limit / stop / conditional / reduce-only variants, buy and sell), fill markers, per-account ghost lines for fan-out, liquidation-estimate line with CMP-227 EstimatedBadge, break-even line, armed/disarmed chrome.
- Interaction states per line: idle · hover (drag handle revealed, ≥24 px) · dragging (ghost line + live price/Δ/R readout + snapped-to-tick indicator) · pending-amend · rejected (spring-back + reason chip) · keyboard-focused (visible focus ring on the DOM-mirrored line) · disabled-because-disarmed (lock cursor + tooltip "One-click trading is off").
- **Legibility over footprint**: specified treatment (halo/scrim, minimum contrast) so trading lines stay readable over dense footprint cells and the heatmap — the SCR-030 sign-off checklist item.
- Chart order entry affordance: the price-axis / price-area affordance for the modifier map chosen in E31-D01, incl. the invalid-side refusal inline explanation (US-ORD-007 scenario 3).
- **SCR-040 Chart trading overlay settings** hi-fi: a toggle per overlay element, the drag-to-modify on/off choice with an explicit written risk note, the "confirm when the new SL is on the wrong side of the mark" copy, and the statement in text that a keyboard alternative exists via SCR-064.
- Undo affordance: the toast/inline control, its dwell time, and what it says after the underlying order already filled.
- All copy strings written (not lorem), including the wrong-side confirm and the snapped-to-tick tooltip ("Snapped to 0.5 tick").
- Light and dark themes, comfortable and compact density, per `16-design-system-brief.md`.

## Out of scope
Visual design (E31-D02/D03). Hotkey remapping UI (E30/SET). Any implementation.

DOM ladder affordances (E31-D03). Order ticket form (E30 designs). Motion spec (E31-D04). Implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Modifier conflict resolved
  Given the catalogue and the story text disagree on the chart-trading modifier map
  When research completes
  Then one map is chosen, recorded in a decision table, and both documents are updated to match

Scenario: Undo expectation quantified
  Then the research states a recommended undo window in seconds with the evidence behind it,
  and states what happens to an order that already filled inside that window

Scenario: Participants could not complete a dangerous action accidentally
  Given the think-aloud sessions on the demo environment
  Then every observed accidental-trigger moment is logged with the condition that caused it
  and maps to a mitigation in the hi-fi brief
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Every overlay element is drawn in every state
  Given the SCR-040 element list
  Then each element has idle, hover, dragging, pending, rejected, keyboard-focused and disarmed frames

Scenario: Legibility proven, not asserted
  Given a frame with the densest footprint and the heatmap behind the trading lines
  Then measured contrast of every line, label and handle meets WCAG 2.2 AA non-text contrast (3:1)
  and the check is recorded on the frame

Scenario: Danger is never silent
  Given a drag that would place a stop on the wrong side of the mark
  Then the frames show the confirm dialog with the exact catalogue copy and a cancel that leaves the stop untouched

Scenario: Drag is never the only way
  Then SCR-040 states in visible text that SL/TP can be edited from SCR-064 by keyboard,
  and the chart line frames show the keyboard-focus and arrow-step affordance
```

## Technical notes / design
Sessions run against **demo only**. Use the existing R2 builds; no prototype build is required. Record sessions with consent; store notes in the design repo, never trading credentials.

Trading lines live on their own engine layer (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §4) with a ≤2 ms redraw budget; designs must not require per-frame text reflow of more than the handful of labels on screen. Snap granularity is the instrument `tickSize` from `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}`.

## Test plan
N/A (research). Validation is the Owner's sign-off on the modifier-map decision table.

Design review by the CDO plus a build-feasibility review by the chart-engine lead (confirming label/halo cost fits the 2 ms budget). Contrast measurements attached.

## Security notes
Sessions must not use live accounts or real API keys; screen recordings are reviewed for key/token leakage before storage (`04-security-program.md` data-handling rules). Data classification: internal.

Frames must show the environment badge (demo/live) on every trading-capable surface — no trading control may be drawn without both the arm state and the environment visible (R3 rule restated from E30). Ghost lines must not expose account labels a `viewer` role may not see.

## Accessibility notes
Include at least one session probing the keyboard-only path expectation, since every drag must have a keyboard equivalent (`05-accessibility-standard.md`); capture what keyboard users expect "commit" to be (Enter) and "abandon" (Esc).

Specify the DOM-mirror for CMP-192: each line focusable, arrow keys step by tick, Enter commits, Esc abandons, Delete removes with a ConfirmDialog above a configurable notional threshold. Announcements for pending/acknowledged/rejected are drafted here as copy.

## Performance notes
Capture perceived-latency expectations for click→visible acknowledgement, to sanity-check budget #4 (ack p95 <300 ms) as a *felt* number.

No design element may require more than the ≤2 ms overlay redraw; the dragging readout must be a single composited label, not a per-frame re-layout of the axis.

## Observability
N/A.

Specify which interactions emit `chart.trading_overlay_changed`, `trading.chart_drag_modify_enabled` (audited on LIVE) so engineering wires the right events.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Sessions run and synthesised; findings doc merged.
- [ ] Modifier-map decision table signed off by the Owner and the CDO.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030/SCR-040 and `11-user-stories.md` US-ORD-007 updated to one consistent map.
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed for anything discovered outside E31 scope.
- [ ] Presented at Design Review.

- [ ] All frames + states in Figma, linked from the SCR-030/SCR-040 catalogue entries.
- [ ] SCR-040 design sign-off acceptance checklist (all four items) ticked.
- [ ] Contrast measurements recorded; a11y designer consulted.
- [ ] Copy reviewed for the advice-boundary rule (no recommendation language).
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded; ticket Status Done by end of Sprint 15.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E21** (the DOM ladder and chart surfaces this research observes traders using).

Merges the former E31-D01 (research) and E31-D02 (chart-layer hi-fi) into one design deliverable so the epic's design spend fits the 26-point roadmap budget for E31 (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2).

**Design-ahead:** must reach Status Done by the end of **Sprint 14** — three sprints ahead of the first consuming FE story (E31-S01, Sprint 17), satisfying the ≥2-sprint design-ahead rule in `00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence.

title: Hi-fi DOM trading, design-system, motion spec and a11y review
body:
## Context
E21 shipped SCR-050 as a *readable* ladder with trading affordances rendered disabled. E31 turns them on (US-DOM-007 click-to-trade, US-DOM-008 drag-to-modify) and adds the destructive one-click actions (US-ORD-010 flatten/cancel-all, US-ORD-011 reverse) whose confirmations live on SCR-072 and SCR-076.

E31 changes the contract of several catalogued components rather than inventing one-offs: CMP-192 OrderLineOverlay gains drag/pending/rejected states, CMP-229 ArmToggle gains the `chart` and `dom` scopes in their armed-live form, CMP-230 OwnOrderMarker gains drag and cancel affordances, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog gains the flatten/reverse variants. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 forbids ad hoc components — every new state must be a design-system entry with tokens, Storybook stories and tests.

This epic's entire value proposition is pointer-driven, which is precisely the pattern `05-accessibility-standard.md` refuses to allow as an only-path. R3's quality gate requires the DOM ladder to be fully keyboard-operable and danger/confirm patterns to be announced. This review certifies the designs *before* build, so a11y is not retrofitted in Sprint 18.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-050 trading states**: armed vs locked ladder chrome (CMP-229 ArmToggle, scope `dom`); per-row hover target showing what a click will do ("Limit buy 0.1 @ 64 100"); Ctrl-hover showing the market variant; own-order markers (CMP-230) in the dedicated "Your orders" column with cancel affordance; drag-a-marker-to-another-row states (grab, drag, drop-valid, drop-invalid, pending, rejected/return-to-origin).
- Disarmed behaviour frames: a click opens a **pre-filled ticket** (hand-off frame to E30's SCR-060) instead of firing.
- Escape = cancel-all-on-symbol affordance and its confirm.
- **SCR-072 Kill-switch / freeze confirmation** variant for flatten-symbol / flatten-group / cancel-all: per-account result list, "retried once automatically" reporting, and the "nothing to flatten" no-op state.
- **SCR-076 Order confirmation modal** variant for **reverse**: restates current position, resulting position, the doubled quantity, the fresh stop that will attach (CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice), margin required vs available, and — per US-ORD-011 — reverse **always** confirms even when armed.
- Error frames: exchange rejection (hand-off to SCR-077 rejection drawer), already-filled cancel translated to "Already filled", insufficient margin refusal *before* sending.
- Row-target sizing spec ≥24 px at every supported density; hit-target diagram.
- Copy for every message, light/dark, both densities.

- Design-system updates in Figma + `15-component-catalogue.md` entries for **CMP-192, CMP-229, CMP-230, CMP-044, CMP-158, CMP-232, CMP-130**: new props/variants, token usage (`color.order.line`, `color.position.entry/sl/tp`, `color.status.danger`, `radius.pill`, `font.mono`), and the Storybook story list each must ship with.
- Any genuinely new token proposals (e.g. a pending/optimistic state colour and a spring-back treatment) raised against `16-design-system-brief.md` with contrast evidence — reuse first, add only with design-system team approval.
- **Motion spec**: drag follow (1:1, no easing), snap-to-tick settle, pending pulse, spring-back on reject, undo-toast enter/exit, confirmation dialog enter. Durations, easings, and the **reduced-motion** equivalents (`prefers-reduced-motion`: no pulse, instant state change, still clearly distinguishable without motion).
- Explicit rule: motion never encodes state alone — every animated state also has a static text/shape cue (colour-independence + motion-independence).

- Review of the E31-D02/D03/D04 artefacts against `05-accessibility-standard.md` (WCAG 2.2 AA) covering:
  - **2.1.1 / 2.5.7**: every drag has a non-drag equivalent — chart line: focus → arrow keys (tick step) → Enter commit / Esc abandon; ladder marker: row action menu → "Move my order" → arrow keys → Enter.
  - **2.5.8 target size**: ≥24 px for line handles, ladder rows and marker cancel affordances at every density.
  - **1.4.11 non-text contrast** for lines, handles, focus rings over footprint/heatmap backgrounds.
  - **4.1.2 / 4.1.3**: roles and live-region strategy for pending / acknowledged / rejected / auto-disarm announcements; politeness levels; no announcement storms during a drag (throttle to on-commit + on-resolve).
  - **3.2.5 / 3.3.4**: destructive actions are confirmable/reversible — the undo window and the confirm policy.
  - **1.4.1** colour independence: buy/sell and SL/TP never colour-only; glyph/label always present.
  - Focus management in and out of SCR-072/SCR-076 dialogs; focus return to the originating line/row.
- A written sign-off note with any blocking findings recorded as changes to D02/D03/D04 before they can be marked Done.
- Screen-reader script: the exact utterances for the six key moments (focus line, begin keyboard reposition, commit, pending, acknowledged, rejected).

## Out of scope
Ladder rendering, heatmap, depth tiers, colour scale (E21 designs). Chart layer (E31-D02). Motion (E31-D04).

Screen-level layout (D02/D03). Implementation of the Storybook stories (the consuming engineering stories own that).

Automated auditing of the built product (E31-Q05). Non-E31 chart surfaces.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A click's consequence is visible before it happens
  Given the ladder is armed and the pointer rests on a bid row
  Then the hover frame states side, type, resolved quantity and price in words before any click

Scenario: Disarmed never fires
  Given the ladder is locked
  Then the frames show a click opening a pre-filled confirmation ticket, never a submission

Scenario: Reverse cannot be one-clicked
  Then the reverse flow always routes through the SCR-076 variant, with no "don't ask again" for LIVE,
  and the resulting stop is shown explicitly

Scenario: Flatten reports per account
  Given a trade group of three accounts and one failing leg
  Then the SCR-072 variant frame shows per-account outcomes, the automatic single retry, and the residual failure with a next action
```

```gherkin
Scenario: No one-off components
  Given the E31 frames
  Then every trading control maps to a catalogued CMP-* entry with its new variants documented

Scenario: Reduced motion is equivalent, not degraded
  Given prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  Then every state the motion spec conveys is still conveyed by a static cue, verified frame by frame

Scenario: Tokens, not hex values
  Then no new frame uses a raw colour value that is not a design token, or the token is proposed and approved here
```

```gherkin
Scenario: No drag-only path survives review
  Given every interactive affordance in the E31 designs
  Then each has a documented keyboard path, and any that does not blocks design sign-off

Scenario: Announcements are specified verbatim
  Then the review produces the literal strings a screen reader will speak for pending, acknowledged and rejected states

Scenario: Targets measured
  Then handle and row target sizes are measured at compact density and each is ≥24 px, or the density is adjusted
```

## Technical notes / design
Own-order markers come from the `orders` / `positions` WS topics filtered to the visible price window (CMP-230 data contract); drag-to-modify issues `PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`. Flatten uses `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/close` (reduce-only market) and `POST /api/v1/orders/cancel-all`; reverse uses `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/reverse`.

Pending state must be distinguishable from acknowledged state without colour (e.g. dashed line + "pending" label), because red/green already carry side semantics.

Accept the SCR-064 modal as the *richer* keyboard alternative for SL/TP, but the inline arrow-key path must still exist on the line itself — SCR-064 is not a substitute for 2.1.1 on the overlay.

## Test plan
Design review + a walkthrough with QA to confirm every state in the frames is observable/testable; feeds E31-Q01's black-box plan directly.

Design-system review; the token proposals go through the normal DS intake. Contrast and non-text-contrast checks on every new variant.

Manual review with a screen-reader user (NVDA + VoiceOver) walking the prototype/redlines; findings logged with WCAG SC references.

## Security notes
Destructive controls must be unreachable for `viewer` role — draw the RBAC-disabled state. Environment badge mandatory on the ladder header. Confirmation copy must never be dismissible by a single Enter pass-through (the 400 ms guard from SCR-076).

The armed-LIVE variant must be unmistakable at a glance (R3 rule: no trading control operable unless arm state *and* environment are visible) — reviewed jointly with Security.

Confirm that keyboard paths cannot bypass the arm/lock gate or the confirm policy — a keyboard shortcut must not be a faster route to an unconfirmed order than the mouse.

## Accessibility notes
Ladder is a `role="grid"` with roving tabindex (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §4.2); Enter on a focused row opens a row action menu containing every mouse action (place limit / place market / cancel my order / move my order). Confirmations are `alertdialog` with focus trapped and the action restated in the button's accessible name. Drag must have the keyboard "move my order → arrow keys → Enter" equivalent drawn.

Each variant ships an accessible-name pattern (e.g. ArmToggle: "Chart trading: locked"); announcement politeness levels specified (assertive for arming in live and for rejections, polite for pending).

This ticket *is* the a11y note; output is the normative spec the engineering stories implement.

## Performance notes
Hover previews must be computed from already-loaded state (no fetch); the row-action menu must open ≤80 ms.

Motion must be compositor-only (transform/opacity) so it cannot cost chart frame budget.

Announcement throttling exists partly for performance: live-region churn during a 60 fps drag is both an AT and a main-thread hazard.

## Observability
Specify `dom.click_trade`, `dom.drag_amend`, `position.flattened`, `position.reversed` event payload fields the frames imply (price row, modifier, resolved qty, account).

N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Frames complete for armed/locked, all drag states, all confirmations, all errors, both densities and themes.
- [ ] SCR-072 and SCR-076 catalogue sign-off checklists ticked for the new variants.
- [ ] RBAC-disabled and disconnected states drawn.
- [ ] CDO sign-off; Done by end of Sprint 15.

- [ ] Catalogue entries updated in `15-component-catalogue.md` with new variants and story lists.
- [ ] Motion spec merged into `16-design-system-brief.md` motion section with reduced-motion equivalents.
- [ ] Token additions approved or explicitly avoided.
- [ ] Design-system team + CDO sign-off.

- [ ] Review completed against every applicable SC with a pass/fail per criterion.
- [ ] Blocking findings fixed in D02/D03/D04 and re-reviewed.
- [ ] Screen-reader utterance script merged into the SCR-030/SCR-050 catalogue a11y sections.
- [ ] Accessibility lead sign-off recorded.

## Dependencies

Merges the former E31-D03 (DOM ladder hi-fi + flatten/reverse confirmations), E31-D04 (design-system contributions + motion spec) and E31-D05 (accessibility design review) so the design track fits E31's 26-point roadmap budget.

**Design-ahead / design-system rule.** *All* design-system contributions for E31 — the CMP-192, CMP-229, CMP-230, CMP-044, CMP-158, CMP-232 and CMP-130 variant, token and motion additions — land **here, in Sprint 15**, i.e. **two sprints before** the earliest consuming FE stories (E31-S01 / E31-S04, Sprint 17) and three before E31-S02/S05/S06 (Sprint 18). title: Prove drag latency, overlay hit-testing and the trading-layer frame budget
body:
## Context
E31 puts *trading-critical, never-sheddable* content onto a canvas that is already at its frame budget with 100k bars, footprint and a 200-depth heatmap (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.2, §4). Two engineering unknowns must be settled before E31-T01 fixes the architecture:

1. **Hit-testing**: can the engine resolve "which order line / which ladder row is under the pointer" within the pointer-event budget while lines overlap drawings and footprint cells (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.9)?
2. **Latency**: US-DOM-007 and US-ORD-006 demand click→submit ≤50 ms client-side. Is that achievable when the pointer event must cross from the canvas/worker boundary into React state and out to `fetch`?

Timebox: **3 days**, agreed with the Architect.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Prototype (throwaway) on the R2 engine build measuring, on the reference machine:
  - pointerdown → intent resolved (side, type, price snapped to tick, resolved qty) in ms, p50/p95, under (a) idle chart, (b) worst case: 100k bars + footprint + heatmap + 20 order lines + live ladder.
  - overlay layer redraw cost per frame with 1, 5, 20 and 50 lines (SCR-040 budget: ≤2 ms).
  - drag follow latency (pointermove → line repositioned on screen) and whether it holds at 60 fps while the shedding ladder is active.
- Determine where drag state must live: main thread vs worker (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §6 worker/OffscreenCanvas protocol) — a drag that round-trips to a worker per move may miss the budget.
- Determine the hit-test strategy: spatial index over line prices vs. GPU picking vs. DOM-mirror elements as the hit surface (the DOM mirror already exists for a11y — reusing it may be both cheapest and most accessible).
- Confirm that trading-line updates can be exempted from the shedding ladder without breaking the ladder's guarantees.

## Out of scope
Production code, visual polish, any order actually being sent (measure to the point of `fetch` call, then stub).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Latency question answered with numbers
  Given the worst-case scene
  Then p50 and p95 for pointerdown -> intent-resolved are recorded, and the result states whether the 50 ms client-side budget holds

Scenario: Overlay budget answered
  Then redraw cost at 1/5/20/50 lines is recorded against the 2 ms budget, with the line count at which it is exceeded

Scenario: A decision, not just data
  Then an ADR records the chosen hit-test strategy and drag-state location, and states the fallback if the budget fails
  (e.g. cap concurrently drawn lines with an explicit "N more orders" affordance)
```

## Technical notes / design
Measure with `performance.now()` around the real event path, and with the Chrome tracing timeline for frame attribution. Test in both Electron (primary shell) and plain Chromium. Reference machine per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Test plan
Benchmark harness only; results reproducible by a checked-in script under `packages/chart-engine/bench/`. No coverage requirement (spike).

## Security notes
Prototype must be hard-wired to a stub submit function; it must not carry any credential or reach any exchange endpoint, not even demo.

## Accessibility notes
If the DOM-mirror is chosen as the hit surface, record the implications for focus order and for the a11y mirror's sync guarantee (`06-...` §4.3 forbids desyncing the mirror from what is rendered).

## Performance notes
This ticket *is* the performance investigation; its numbers become the baseline assertions in E31-Q03.

## Observability
Propose the metric names E31-T01 should emit: `cv_chart_trade_click_to_submit_ms`, `cv_trading_overlay_redraw_ms`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All three questions answered with recorded evidence.
- [ ] **ADR-0017 chart-trading interaction & hit-testing** written in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (even if the decision is "defer").
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed for whichever path was chosen, with findings linked.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated for R2 render performance.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review; prototype branch archived unmerged.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E11** (chart engine interaction loop and hit-testing) and **E21** (the rendered DOM ladder) — both complete well before R3 opens, so this spike runs in **Sprint 16**, strictly ahead of the S17–S18 E31 train window (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2).

**Why this spike deliberately does *not* depend on E29/E30/E32/E39.** It is a rendering-and-input-latency experiment only: it drags a *fake* overlay against recorded data and submits nothing. It uses a stubbed intent sink — no API keys, no OMS, no live account — so it cannot be blocked by the order-placing stack. The real dependencies on **E29** (OMS + private WS), **E30** (arm/lock, confirm policy, hotkeys), **E32** (native-SL invariant) and **E39** (risk caps, kill-switch) are carried by **E31-T01** and by the individual stories, each of which is scheduled strictly *after* the sprint in which its blocker completes — see the epic's Dependency graph table. title: Test plan and E2E suite for chart and DOM trading
body:
## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes QA sign-off non-skippable for every Story. E31 spans six interaction surfaces with heavy state coupling (arm state, environment, kill-switch, risk lockouts, RBAC role, book freshness, connection state), so the plan must be written from the specification (E31-D06 handoff) before the build, not derived from the implementation afterwards.

R3's E2E quality gate explicitly names "chart trading, DOM trading" among the Playwright web + Electron flows that must exist. These are the automated proof that the direct-manipulation surfaces behave — and, critically, the automated proof of R3 exit criterion 2: that **no path** can open a position without a native stop.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A black-box plan covering US-ORD-007, US-ORD-008, US-ORD-009, US-ORD-010, US-ORD-011, US-DOM-007, US-DOM-008 across SCR-030, SCR-040, SCR-050, SCR-063, SCR-064, SCR-072, SCR-076, SCR-077.
- **State matrix** to be exercised for every action: {armed, disarmed} × {demo} × {kill-switch on/off} × {lockout on/off} × {owner, manager, viewer} × {book fresh, stale, resynchronising, disconnected} — with the expected outcome stated per cell (submit / refuse-with-reason / open-ticket / hard-disabled) so testers are never guessing.
- Per-story scenario scripts including every Gherkin failure case: invalid side/price, amend rejected, drag through price, already-filled cancel, nothing to flatten, insufficient margin on reverse, partial flatten-group failure, late/absent WS acknowledgement.
- Boundary catalogue: tick-size rounding at the half tick, min-lot boundaries, percent-preset resolution with stale wallet data, notional threshold for the delete confirm, undo window at expiry ±1 s, 24 px targets at compact density.
- Data setup: demo accounts, a 3-account trade group, a symbol with a coarse tick size and one with a fine tick size, a pre-seeded position and pre-seeded working orders.
- Defect-reporting conventions: any missing native stop, any action possible while disarmed/kill-switched, and any silent partial success are `priority/p0-critical` by definition.
- Entry/exit criteria for the QA pass and the traceability table story → scenario → test case id.

- Playwright specs (web **and** Electron shell) under the existing E2E project, against **demo**:
  1. **Chart click** → limit placed at the tick-snapped price → line renders → order visible via the API → cancel from the chart.
  2. **Chart drag** → amend → exchange price matches → undo within the window restores the original price.
  3. **Chart drag refusal** → stop dragged through price → assert **zero** order-amend network requests (network-level assertion, not a UI assertion).
  4. **DOM click** → limit at a bid row → own-order marker appears → drag to another row → price matches → cancel from the marker.
  5. **Disarmed** → chart click and ladder click each open a pre-filled ticket and submit nothing.
  6. **Flatten** → position + two working orders → flatten → both cancelled and position closed, reported as one operation.
  7. **Flatten no-op** → nothing open → assert zero network calls and the "nothing to flatten" message.
  8. **Reverse** → long → reverse → resulting short with a fresh native stop, confirmation mandatory even when armed.
  9. **Safety sweep (the exit-criterion test)**: parameterised over every E31 entry path (chart click, chart drag, DOM click, DOM drag, flatten, reverse) asserting that (a) every position-opening action results in a native exchange-side stop, and (b) the action is refused while disarmed, while kill-switched and while locked out. Zero escapes.
  10. **RBAC**: a `viewer` session cannot operate any E31 affordance; a forced API call returns 403 with no state change and an audit row.
- Deterministic fixtures and helpers: demo account seeding, position/order seeding and teardown, a helper asserting "no request matched this endpoint", and a helper reading the audit log to assert provenance fields.
- Stability requirements: no arbitrary sleeps — wait on the private WS events; each spec idempotent and re-runnable; tagged so the safety sweep can run as a **required check** on PRs touching `area/oms-execution`.

## Out of scope
Writing automation (E31-Q02). Performance scripting (E31-Q03). A11y audit (E31-Q05).

Perf/load (Q03), chaos (Q04), a11y automation (Q05), unit/component tests (owned by the stories).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every story scenario has a test case
  Given the seven user stories and their Gherkin scenarios
  Then each scenario maps to at least one numbered manual test case, including every failure scenario

Scenario: The state matrix is exhaustive and decided
  Then every cell of the state matrix has a stated expected outcome, with no "TBD"

Scenario: The plan is executable by someone who did not write it
  Given a tester new to the epic
  Then they can set up the data and execute the plan from the document alone
```

```gherkin
Scenario: All ten flows green in both shells
  Given the Playwright suite on web and Electron against demo
  Then all ten specs pass, three consecutive runs, with no flakes

Scenario: Safety sweep is a gate
  Given a deliberately broken build in which one path skips the native stop
  Then the safety sweep fails and blocks the merge queue

Scenario: Refusals are proven at the network layer
  Given the refusal specs
  Then they assert the absence of the corresponding network request, not merely the presence of an error message

Scenario: Provenance asserted
  Given a DOM click-trade
  Then the suite reads back the audit record and asserts source, modifier and price row
```

## Technical notes / design
Execute exclusively against **staging (demo)** per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 — never live. Use the demo environment's REST-only order-entry constraint as a deliberate test condition.

Demo has **no WS order entry** (REST only) — the suite must not assume WS submission. Acknowledgements still arrive on the private WS topics and are the correct thing to await.

Run the suite against a dedicated demo sub-account so parallel CI runs cannot interfere; serialise the safety sweep if account state contention is observed.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* the plan; its own validation is a review by the SDET lead and the E31 engineering lead confirming testability of every case.

Self-referential: the suite's own reliability is validated by three consecutive clean runs and by the deliberately-broken-build check for the safety sweep.

## Security notes
The plan must include the security-relevant negative cases (disarmed, kill-switched, locked out, viewer role, out-of-scope account) as first-class test cases, not as a security-team-only concern; results feed E31-X03.

Credentials for the demo accounts come from the CI secret store, never from the repo; the suite must fail closed if it detects a `live` environment target. Add an explicit assertion at suite start that `environment === 'demo'`.

## Accessibility notes
The plan includes keyboard-only execution of the full happy path for each surface as a mandatory case (the detailed audit remains E31-Q05).

At least the chart-click and DOM-click flows must have a keyboard-only variant in the suite, so the keyboard paths are regression-protected rather than only manually checked.

## Performance notes
Includes the felt-latency observations (click→visible acknowledgement) as a qualitative case, with the measured version in E31-Q03.

Suite wall-clock ≤12 min in CI; the safety sweep alone ≤4 min so it is viable as a required check.

## Observability
Each test case states which audit event should exist afterwards, so testers verify auditing as part of functional testing.

Suite emits per-spec timings; failures attach the correlation ids of the orders involved so backend logs can be joined.

title: Perf, chaos and a11y audit plus QA sign-off for chart & DOM trading
body:
## Context
E31 carries three hard numbers: click→submit ≤50 ms client-side, click→ack p95 <300 ms on demo (budget #4), and a ≤2 ms trading-overlay redraw with trading data exempt from the shedding ladder (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3, §5). These must be measured in CI, not asserted in a ticket.

R3's Chaos gate requires "WS kill mid-order, backend restart mid-TWAP, Postgres failover mid-fan-out — all resume to a correct, reconciled state". E31's contribution is the *direct-manipulation* half: what happens to an optimistic drag, a pending click-trade or a half-finished flatten when the world breaks underneath it. The failure mode being hunted is a UI that shows a settled state the exchange never agreed to.

R3's A11y gate requires the DOM ladder to be fully keyboard-operable and danger/confirm patterns to be announced. E31 is the epic that makes the ladder and the chart *actionable*, so this audit decides whether the R3 gate passes. `05-accessibility-standard.md` grants no "trading tools are special" exemption.

Scripted tests only find the failures someone imagined. E31's danger lies in the combinations nobody wrote down: dragging while the symbol changes, clicking while the arm timer expires, flattening while a fill lands. This ticket adds time-boxed exploratory testing, folds E31 into the standing regression pack, and carries the epic-level QA sign-off required by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Engine benchmark** (extends the existing chart-engine bench harness): overlay redraw cost at 1/5/20/50 order lines, measured under the worst-case scene (100k bars, footprint on, 200-depth heatmap live), in Electron and Chromium, on the reference machine. Asserts ≤2 ms and asserts fps ≥30 floor.
- **Shedding-ladder assertion**: drive the engine into the stress scenario and assert that heatmap cadence and footprint text degrade first while **order-line and position-line updates continue every frame** — the "never acceptable" rule made executable.
- **Client-side interaction latency harness**: instrument pointerdown→`fetch` issued for chart click, chart drag commit, DOM click and DOM drag commit; assert p95 ≤50 ms; publish p50/p95/p99.
- **k6 script** for the order path: sustained click-trade-equivalent order submission against demo at a realistic manual rate and at the per-UID limit, asserting ack p95 <300 ms and correct `10018` back-off behaviour without lost acknowledgements.
- Baseline numbers recorded from E31-K01 promoted into assertions with an agreed regression threshold; results published to the perf dashboard per `06-...` reporting conventions.
- CI wiring: engine benchmark on every PR touching the overlay or the engine; k6 on a nightly schedule against demo.

Chaos scenarios, automated where possible and scripted-manual otherwise, run against demo:
1. **WS dropped mid-amend**: drag commits, REST ack received, WS killed before the order event → assert the marker/line shows *unreconciled* (not settled), reconnect restores truth, and the final rendered price equals the exchange price.
2. **REST times out, order actually placed**: inject a timeout after the exchange accepted → assert the idempotency key prevents a duplicate on retry and the reconciliation loop surfaces the real order rather than an orphan.
3. **Backend restart mid-flatten**: kill the backend between the cancel-all leg and the close leg → assert the UI reports a visible partial state, and after restart the reconciliation shows the true position; assert no silent "flattened" claim.
4. **Exchange 5xx / `10018` storm during click-trading**: assert back-off with jitter, the user-visible rate-limit message, and no lost acknowledgements.
5. **Clock skew**: skew the client clock → assert undo-window timing and stale-book detection degrade safely (fail closed: disable trading affordances rather than trust the clock).
6. **Slow consumer**: force the client into the WS slow-consumer path → assert `orders`/`executions` are never dropped (protocol rule) and the client is disconnected with `4429` rather than shown a wrong position.
7. **Kill-switch flipped mid-drag**: assert the in-flight commit is refused, the line springs back, and the reason is shown.
8. **Disconnect during the undo window**: assert undo is unavailable rather than silently failing, with an honest message.
- Each scenario documents: injection method, expected system behaviour, observable evidence (UI state, audit rows, metrics), and pass criteria.

- **Automated**: axe-core in CI across SCR-030 (trading layer on), SCR-040, SCR-050 (armed and locked), SCR-063, SCR-064, SCR-072, SCR-076 — zero serious/critical violations, with any accepted exception documented and approved.
- **Manual screen-reader passes** with NVDA + Chrome/Electron and VoiceOver + Safari/Chrome, covering:
  - Placing an order from the chart by keyboard; repositioning a line by arrow keys; committing and abandoning.
  - Ladder grid navigation with roving tabindex; opening the row action menu; placing, moving and cancelling by keyboard.
  - Flatten, cancel-all and reverse confirmations: focus trap, focus return, action restated in the accessible name, the 400 ms Enter guard.
  - Pending → acknowledged → rejected announcements: correct politeness, no announcement storms during a drag, auto-disarm announced when it fires.
- **Target size** measurement (2.5.8) for line handles, ladder rows and marker cancel affordances at every density; **non-text contrast** (1.4.11) for lines/handles/focus rings measured over dense footprint and an active heatmap.
- **Colour independence** (1.4.1): buy/sell, SL/TP and pending state each verified distinguishable in greyscale and with a deuteranopia simulation.
- **Reduced motion**: all E31 motion verified to degrade per the D04 spec with state still conveyed.
- **DOM-mirror parity**: verify the accessible mirror matches rendered state, including under the shedding ladder (cross-check with E31-Q03's parity assertion).
- Findings logged per WCAG SC with severity; blockers must be fixed before the epic's DoD.

- **Exploratory charters** (2 hours each, session-based, with notes and any defect filed immediately):
  1. "Race the state": change symbol, switch account/trade group, let the arm timer expire, toggle environment and flip the kill-switch *while* drags and click-trades are in flight.
  2. "Fat fingers": rapid repeated clicks, click-and-micro-drag, drag off-canvas, drag onto another pane, double-click, middle-click, touch/trackpad gestures, browser zoom at 200 %.
  3. "Fills during interaction": arrange for fills and partial fills to land during a drag, during a pending amend and during a flatten.
  4. "Multi-pane and multi-window": two charts on the same symbol, chart plus ladder on the same symbol, Electron second window — assert overlays and pending state stay consistent everywhere.
  5. "Undo boundaries": undo at the window's edge, undo after a partial fill, undo twice, undo after the symbol changed.
- **Regression pack additions**: the E31 smoke path (place from chart, drag, cancel, DOM place, flatten) added to the standing pre-release regression suite, plus the safety sweep referenced as a required gate.
- **Epic-level QA sign-off**: execute the E31-Q01 black-box plan end to end on the release candidate build, record pass/fail per scenario, confirm all E31 tickets' QA sign-offs exist, and confirm no open P0/P1 defects in E31 scope.
- A short QA report for the R3 PRR evidence pack.

## Out of scope
Backend ingestion/fan-out load (E17/E21/E34 scripts). Chaos (Q04).

Backend-internal failover mechanics (E45 owns reconciliation/chaos at large; this ticket is the E31 surface behaviour and feeds E45's suite).

Design-stage review (E31-D05, already done) and non-E31 chart surfaces.

Fixing defects (they route to the owning story or a new Bug). Non-E31 regression content.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Overlay budget enforced
  Given the worst-case scene with 20 order lines
  Then the measured overlay redraw is at most 2 ms and the benchmark fails the build if it regresses beyond the agreed threshold

Scenario: Trading data is never shed
  Given the engine is driven into the stress scenario
  Then heatmap cadence and footprint text degrade, order and position lines still update every frame,
  and the test fails if a trading-line update is dropped

Scenario: Interaction latency measured, not estimated
  Then p50, p95 and p99 for pointerdown to request-issued are published per surface, and p95 is at most 50 ms

Scenario: Order ack budget holds under load
  Given the k6 profile at the per-UID limit
  Then ack p95 is under 300 ms, no acknowledgement is lost, and 10018 back-off is observed with jitter
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Never a false settled state
  Given any injected failure in any of the eight scenarios
  Then the UI never displays an order or position state that the exchange did not confirm

Scenario: No duplicate orders from retries
  Given a REST timeout on an order that was actually accepted
  Then no duplicate order exists on the exchange after the client's retry behaviour completes

Scenario: Partial flatten is visible
  Given the backend dies between the cancel and close legs
  Then the user sees an explicit partial state with a next action, never a success message

Scenario: Fail closed on clock skew
  Given a skewed client clock
  Then trading affordances disable with a stated reason rather than acting on untrustworthy timing
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Zero critical automated violations
  Given axe-core over the seven screens in their trading-enabled states
  Then there are no serious or critical violations, or each has a documented, approved exception

Scenario: Full keyboard operation proven
  Given a keyboard-only user
  Then they can place, reprice, cancel, flatten and reverse from both the chart and the ladder,
  with every outcome announced

Scenario: No drag-only functionality
  Then every pointer-driven capability in E31 has a verified keyboard equivalent, evidenced by a recorded pass

Scenario: Targets and contrast measured
  Then every interactive target is at least 24 px at compact density and every line/handle/focus ring
  meets 3:1 non-text contrast over the worst-case background
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Charters executed with evidence
  Given the five charters
  Then each has a session sheet with notes, coverage areas touched and defects raised

Scenario: No open P0/P1 at sign-off
  Given the epic-level pass
  Then no P0 or P1 defect remains open in E31 scope, or sign-off is withheld

Scenario: Regression pack updated
  Then the E31 smoke path runs as part of the standing pre-release regression and passes on the candidate build

Scenario: Sign-off is recorded per scenario
  Then the black-box plan shows an explicit pass or fail for every numbered case, with the tester and build id
```

## Technical notes / design
Measure on the reference machine defined in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; record GPU/driver and shell versions with every result, since R8 browser/GPU compatibility is a live risk.

The k6 script must use demo credentials from the secret store and must be rate-aware — the point is to prove the governor, not to trip the exchange into punishing the account.

Injection via the existing test proxy/toxiproxy-style layer for WS and REST, container restarts for the backend, and a clock-offset harness for the client. Every run captures the audit log slice and the relevant metrics window as evidence.

Test in the Electron shell as the primary environment (it is the primary shell) *and* in a browser, because AT behaviour differs; record versions of AT, OS and shell with every result.

All execution on demo, on the release-candidate build, in both web and Electron. Session notes follow the team's session-based test management format.

## Test plan
The scripts are the tests; their validity is checked by injecting a known 5 ms artificial delay into the overlay path and confirming the benchmark detects it.

Each scenario is a scripted run with a written expected/actual record; the four automatable ones (1, 2, 4, 7) join the nightly chaos job.

Automated axe run in CI plus a scripted manual protocol per surface; each manual pass produces a recording and a findings sheet keyed to WCAG SCs.

## Security notes
Scripts must be hard-guarded to demo; a live target must abort the run. No credential appears in the results or the dashboard. Load generation must not be usable as an unauthenticated tool — it authenticates through the normal session path.

Chaos runs are demo-only and must not disable the safety invariant as part of the injection — a scenario that would place an unprotected position is itself a failure to report, not a test setup step. Verify audit continuity across restarts (the hash-chained `audit_log` must remain verifiable).

Confirm that keyboard/AT paths enforce the same arm, confirm-policy, kill-switch and RBAC gates as pointer paths — an accessibility path must never become a safety bypass. Explicitly test: arming via keyboard in LIVE requires the deliberate second action (CMP-229 spec).

Charters must include at least one deliberate attempt to trade while disarmed, kill-switched, locked out and as `viewer`; any success is a `priority/p0-critical` security defect routed to E31-X03 immediately rather than merely filed.

## Accessibility notes
Assert that the DOM-mirror accessibility layer stays in sync with the rendered state under shedding (`06-...` §4.3 forbids desync) — an automated parity check of mirrored line prices vs rendered line prices.

Assert that degraded/unreconciled/disconnected states are announced, not merely styled, since these are exactly the moments a user most needs to be told something changed.

This ticket is the accessibility evidence for the epic and for the R3 gate.

One charter session is run keyboard-only to catch a11y regressions the automated audit could miss.

## Performance notes
This ticket is the performance evidence for the epic's DoD and feeds the R3 §7.4 Load gate.

Assert recovery time: after reconnect, the UI reflects true exchange state within the reconciliation loop's stated interval.

Check that live-region updates during drags and high-frequency ladder updates do not cause AT lag; if they do, the throttling from E31-T01/D05 is insufficient and a defect is filed.

Testers record any perceptible stutter or latency and cross-check against E31-Q03's numbers before filing.

## Observability
Results published to the perf dashboard; `cv_trading_overlay_redraw_ms` and `cv_chart_trade_click_to_submit_ms` histograms validated against the harness numbers so production telemetry is trusted.

Every scenario asserts the expected log/metric/audit evidence exists — `cv_trading_unreconciled_total` increments, back-off metrics move, audit rows persist across restart.

N/A (findings are recorded in the QA system).

Sign-off includes a check that audit rows exist for a sample of every action type performed during the pass — auditing is part of the acceptance, not an afterthought.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All four scripts implemented and wired into CI/nightly.
- [ ] Baselines recorded with machine/driver/shell metadata.
- [ ] Injected-regression check proves the benchmarks detect regressions.
- [ ] Results attached to E31 and to the R3 perf evidence pack.
- [ ] Reviewed by the chart-engine lead and the SDET lead.

- [ ] All eight scenarios documented with injection, expectation and evidence.
- [ ] Four automated and wired into the nightly chaos job; four scripted-manual runs executed and recorded.
- [ ] Any defect found filed with `priority/p0-critical` where it involves a false settled state or a duplicate order.
- [ ] Results handed to E45 for inclusion in the broader resilience suite.
- [ ] SDET lead and Architect sign-off.

- [ ] axe-core green in CI across all seven screens in trading-enabled states.
- [ ] NVDA and VoiceOver passes executed and recorded with AT/OS/shell versions.
- [ ] Target-size and contrast measurements recorded.
- [ ] Colour-independence and reduced-motion verified.
- [ ] All blocking findings fixed and re-verified; non-blocking findings filed with priority.
- [ ] Accessibility lead sign-off; result attached to the R3 A11y gate evidence.

- [ ] Five charters executed with session sheets attached.
- [ ] Regression pack updated and green on the candidate.
- [ ] Black-box plan executed with per-scenario results; QA sign-off comment posted on the epic.
- [ ] Zero open P0/P1 in E31 scope.
- [ ] QA report filed for the R3 PRR evidence pack.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E31-Q01** (the test plan and E2E harness these extend), **E31-K01** (the Sprint-16 latency methodology and baseline numbers), **E31-S03 / S05 / S06** (the last functional slices) and **E31-D07** (design-QA findings must be dispositioned before sign-off).

title: Place an order by clicking a price on the chart
body:
## Context
**US-ORD-007 — Order from chart (Must):** *"As a trader, I want to click a chart price to create an order, so that I trade where I analyse."* This is the first of the direct-manipulation stories and establishes the chart trading layer that S02 (dragging) builds on.

The interaction is modifier-driven on SCR-030's price area; the exact map is frozen by E31-D01 and published in the E31-D06 handoff (the story text and the screens catalogue disagreed before that decision, so **implement the handoff table, not either document's original wording**).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Screens**: SCR-030 (chart panel — the trading layer), SCR-040 (the settings modal that toggles working-order lines and the arm-state display), SCR-076 (order confirmation modal when the confirm policy requires it), SCR-077 (rejection drawer on failure).
- **Components**: CMP-192 OrderLineOverlay (the placed order's line), CMP-229 ArmToggle (scope `chart`), CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-130 SlippageEstimateChip, CMP-232 LimitsChip, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge (liquidation line).
- Chart trading layer mount on SCR-030 rendering working orders and the position from the `orders` / `positions` WS topics, filtered to the visible price window; per-account ghost lines when a trade group is the active target.
- Price-area pointer handling producing a `TradeIntent` via `packages/trading-intent` (E31-T01): limit on the correct side, reduce-only stop, and market-at-market per the frozen modifier map, with the price snapped to `tickSize` and the snap surfaced as a tooltip ("Snapped to 0.5 tick").
- Hover preview stating in words what a click will do before it happens.
- Refusal path: an invalid side/price combination is refused inline with an explanation and **nothing is sent** (US-ORD-007 scenario 3).
- Disarmed path: with one-click locked, the click opens a **pre-filled SCR-060 ticket** requiring explicit confirmation, never a submission ("One-click trading is off — press Ctrl+Shift+T to arm").
- SCR-040 wiring for the overlay element toggles this story introduces (working orders, arm-state display, liquidation-estimate line) and the drag-to-modify toggle's *display* (drag itself lands in S02); enabling drag-to-modify on LIVE emits audit `trading.chart_drag_modify_enabled`.
- Keyboard path: focus the price area, move the crosshair with ↑/↓ by tick, and commit an order at the crosshair price with the documented key, subject to the same confirm policy.

## Out of scope
Dragging existing lines (S02). Cancelling from the chart (S03). DOM surfaces (S04/S05). Flatten/reverse (S06). Bracket construction and native-SL attachment logic (E32) — the entry simply carries the profile's SL and the server enforces it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Limit from chart
  Given BTCUSDT on SCR-030, chart trading armed, and a price above the market
  When I use the limit-sell modifier at that price
  Then a limit sell is created at the tick-snapped price with the profile's native stop attached,
  a pending order line appears immediately, and the acknowledgement arrives within 500 ms

Scenario: Stop from chart on a long
  Given an open long position
  When I use the stop modifier at a price below the market
  Then a reduce-only stop order is created at that price and rendered as a stop line

Scenario: Invalid side/price
  Given the chosen price is on the wrong side for the chosen order type
  Then the action is refused with an inline explanation, nothing is sent to the exchange,
  and the refusal is recorded with its reason

Scenario: Disarmed
  Given one-click trading is locked
  When I click a price with a trading modifier
  Then a pre-filled ticket opens requiring explicit confirmation and no order is submitted

Scenario: Kill-switch engaged
  Given the kill-switch is engaged
  Then no chart click can create an order, the reason is shown, and the attempt is logged

Scenario: Exchange rejection
  Given the exchange rejects the order
  Then the pending line disappears, the exact exchange code and message are surfaced,
  the rejection drawer is reachable, and the attempt is journaled and audited

Scenario: Keyboard equivalent
  Given a keyboard user with the chart focused
  When they move the crosshair to a price and press the commit key
  Then the same intent is produced, the same confirm policy applies,
  and the outcome is announced (pending, then acknowledged or rejected)
```

## Technical notes / design
The overlay is a dedicated engine layer above footprint/drawings/indicators and below modals (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §4), with the hit-test strategy chosen in E31-K01/ADR-0017. Lines are DOM-mirrored for a11y and (per the spike's likely finding) the mirror doubles as the hit surface.

Price ↔ pixel conversion uses the shared viewport transform (§3.5); snapping uses the instrument's `priceFilter.tickSize` from the cached `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}`.

Order submission goes through E31-T01 only — this story contains no `fetch` of its own.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: modifier→intent mapping for every entry in the frozen table; price↔pixel and snapping at pane edges; hover-preview text generation; refusal rendering; disarmed hand-off; ghost-line construction for a 3-account group.
- **Component/Storybook**: CMP-192 stories WorkingOrderLine, PendingLine, RejectedLine, DisarmedLock; visual regression in light/dark, both densities, over a dense footprint background.
- **Integration**: against the mock OMS — submit, ack via the `orders` WS topic, line transitions pending→working.
- **E2E (Playwright, web + Electron)**: place a limit from the chart on demo, assert the exchange order id appears and the line renders; attempt an invalid side and assert nothing was sent (network assertion, not just UI); attempt while disarmed and assert a ticket opened instead.
- **Perf**: click→submit p95 ≤50 ms client-side on the worst-case scene; overlay redraw ≤2 ms with 20 lines.
- **A11y**: axe-core on SCR-030 and SCR-040; keyboard-only placement; announcement assertions.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend for touched files.

## Security notes
This is an order-placing path, therefore `security`-labelled by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8. Threats: accidental submission (mitigated by arm gating, confirm policy, hover preview, undo window), privilege escalation (a `viewer` must not be able to place — server re-checks, UI hard-disables), and repudiation (provenance auditing from E31-T01). A manual abuse-case check is required: attempt placement while disarmed, while kill-switched, while locked out, and as a `viewer`, asserting 403/refusal and **no state change** each time. Data classification: financial.

## Accessibility notes
Per E31-D05: crosshair-driven keyboard placement, ≥24 px affordances, focus visible on the DOM-mirrored line, pending/acknowledged/rejected announced with the specified politeness (assertive for rejection), no colour-only encoding of side (glyph + label), and SCR-040 stating in text that keyboard alternatives exist. axe-core must be green on both screens.

## Performance notes
Budgets: click→submit ≤50 ms client-side (US-DOM-007/US-ORD-006 class NFR), click→ack p95 <300 ms on demo (budget #4), overlay redraw ≤2 ms (SCR-040). Trading-line updates are exempt from the shedding ladder (`06-...` §4.3 "never acceptable").

## Observability
`order.submitted` (audited, with provenance `source='chart-click'`, modifier, price), analytics `chart.trade_from_chart`, `chart.trading_overlay_changed`; audit `trading.chart_drag_modify_enabled` when enabled on LIVE. Metric `cv_chart_trade_click_to_submit_ms{source="chart-click"}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests referencing the scenario name.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80 % frontend on touched files; CI gate green.
- [ ] Storybook stories for the new CMP-192 variants published.
