title: Drag order, stop and target lines on the chart to amend
body:
## Context
**US-ORD-008 — Drag order, stop and target lines (Must):** *"As a trader, I want to drag order and TP/SL lines on the chart, so that I manage trades visually."* This is the signature interaction of the epic and the one with the highest fat-finger consequence, so it carries the undo window, the spring-back-on-reject behaviour and a mandatory keyboard equivalent.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Screens**: SCR-030 (drag on the trading layer), SCR-064 Position SL/TP editor (the richer keyboard alternative, reached from a line's context action), SCR-040 (the drag-to-modify enable toggle and its wrong-side confirm copy), SCR-076/SCR-077 as needed.
- **Components**: CMP-192 OrderLineOverlay (drag, pending, rejected, keyboard-reposition, delete-confirm), CMP-119 BracketEditor and CMP-120 TrailingStopEditor (as the SCR-064 content reached from the line), CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice.
- Draggable line kinds: working order (limit/stop/conditional), position SL, position TP. The position **entry** line is never draggable.
- Drag lifecycle: grab (handle ≥24 px) → live ghost line with a readout of price, Δ from entry and resulting R → drop snapped to tick → `PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}` or `PUT /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/tpsl` via E31-T01 → **pending** visual until the `orders`/`positions` WS event confirms → settle, or **spring back** with the exact reason on rejection.
- Refusals before sending: dropping a stop on the wrong side of the current price is refused with an explanation and the stop stays put (US-ORD-008 scenario 3); the SCR-040 wrong-side-of-mark confirm copy applies where the catalogue specifies a confirm rather than a refusal.
- **Native-SL invariant respected**: dragging an SL may move it, never delete it ("Every position keeps a native stop — you can move it, not delete it." — SCR-064 validation text). Deleting a line that represents a live order above a configurable notional threshold requires a ConfirmDialog (CMP-192 spec).
- **Undo window** (E31-T01): after a drag commits, an undo affordance re-amends to the original price; after a fill it explains instead of acting.
- **Keyboard equivalent** (mandatory): Tab cycles order lines on the visible chart, ↑/↓ step by `tickSize` (with a larger modifier step), Enter commits, Esc abandons and restores, Delete removes with confirmation. States announced per the E31-D05 utterance script.
- Multi-line safety: with a scaled-order ladder of 10+ lines, dragging one never moves a sibling; overlapping lines at the same price expose a disambiguation affordance.

## Out of scope
Creating orders (S01), cancelling (S03), DOM drag (S05), bracket child re-sizing semantics and trailing-stop translation (E32), scaled-ladder editing as a group (E32).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Drag to reprice
  Given a working limit order line on SCR-030
  When I drag it to a new price and release
  Then the price is snapped to the tick, an amend is submitted,
  and the line shows a pending state until the orders WS event acknowledges it

Scenario: Drag rejected
  Given the exchange rejects the amend with order_not_amendable
  Then the line springs back to its original price and the exact reason is displayed with a link to the rejection detail

Scenario: Drag stop through price
  Given a long position and its stop line
  When I drag the stop to the wrong side of the current price
  Then the drop is refused with an explanation, nothing is sent, and the stop stays put

Scenario: Stop cannot be deleted
  When I attempt to delete the native stop line of an open position
  Then the action is refused with the invariant explanation and the position keeps its stop

Scenario: Undo an accidental drag
  Given I dragged a working order and the undo window has not elapsed
  When I activate undo
  Then an amend restoring the original price is submitted and the undo itself is audited

Scenario: Undo after fill
  Given the order filled during the undo window
  Then undo does not send a reversing order; it states the order filled and offers the flatten path

Scenario: Keyboard reposition
  Given a keyboard user focuses a stop line
  When they press the up arrow three times and Enter
  Then the stop moves three ticks, the amend is submitted, and pending then acknowledged are announced

Scenario: Drag while disarmed or kill-switched
  Then lines are not draggable, the lock reason is shown on hover and to screen readers, and nothing is sent
```

## Technical notes / design
Drag state lives where E31-K01/ADR-0017 decided; the visual follow must be compositor-cheap so the chart holds 60 fps during a drag under the worst-case scene.

Amend uses `PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`; omitted fields are left unchanged, and the endpoint refuses with `order_not_amendable` when the order is terminal or already has an amend/cancel in flight — that code maps to the "springs back" path with the copy-deck string. SL/TP on a position uses `PUT /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/tpsl`.

Optimistic rendering is a **pending** style (dashed + label), never the settled style, so the user is never shown a confirmed state that the exchange has not confirmed; reconciliation deadline 1 s (E31-T01).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: drag→price math at all zoom levels and log/percent price scales; snapping; wrong-side detection for long and short, stop and TP, with the mark/last/index trigger sources; undo intent construction; keyboard step arithmetic incl. modifier step; invariant refusal for stop deletion.
- **Component**: CMP-192 stories KeyboardRepriceDemo, DeleteConfirmFlow, PendingAmend, SpringBackOnReject; interaction test for keyboard reprice/delete is an explicit CI gate (trading-critical, per the catalogue).
- **Integration**: amend acknowledged / rejected / never-acknowledged (unreconciled) paths against the mock OMS with recorded Bybit fixtures.
- **E2E**: drag a working order on demo and assert the exchange reflects the new price; drag a stop to the wrong side and assert zero network calls; undo a drag and assert the restoring amend.
- **Perf**: 60 fps sustained during a drag on the worst-case scene; overlay redraw ≤2 ms with 20 lines; a scaled ladder of 10+ lines dragged individually without sibling movement.
- **A11y**: axe-core; NVDA/VoiceOver pass over the reposition flow; target-size verification at compact density.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Order-modifying path → `security`-labelled. Threats: unintended amend from a stray pointer (arm gate, ≥24 px handles, undo window, pending-not-settled rendering), removal of protective stops (invariant refusal client-side plus server enforcement in E32 — client refusal is convenience, the server is the control), repudiation (every drag audited with `source='chart-drag'` and both the old and new price). Abuse-case check: attempt to delete an SL by every available route (drag off-screen, delete key, context menu, API replay) and assert refusal + audit.

## Accessibility notes
2.1.1 and 2.5.7 compliance is the gate: no functionality is drag-only. Announcements throttled to commit and resolve moments — never per pointermove. Focus returns to the line after any dialog. Reduced-motion honours the D04 spec (no spring animation; instant restore with a static cue).

## Performance notes
Drag follow must not exceed one frame of latency; trading overlays are never shed under the §4.3 ladder; the readout label must be a single composited element.

## Observability
Audit `order.amend_requested` / `position.stop_modified` / `position.tp_ladder_set` with old and new price and provenance `source='chart-drag'`; analytics `chart.drag_amend`, `trading.undo_used`; metrics `cv_trading_overlay_redraw_ms`, `cv_trading_unreconciled_total`.

- [ ] axe-core green; manual SR pass; target sizes verified.
- [ ] Perf benchmarks recorded (fps during drag, overlay redraw).
- [ ] Security review + abuse-case results recorded.
- [ ] Design QA (E31-D07) passed.

title: Cancel orders from the chart and the DOM ladder
body:
## Context
**US-ORD-009 — Cancel order from chart and DOM (Should):** *"As a trader, I want to cancel an order by right-clicking or pressing a key on its marker, so that cancellation is as fast as placement."* Cancellation must be at least as fast and as reachable as placement, or the direct-manipulation surfaces become a one-way risk ratchet.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Screens**: SCR-040 (the chart trading overlay settings where the cancel behaviour and cancel-all key are described), SCR-050 (ladder marker cancel), SCR-030 (chart line cancel), SCR-072 (confirmation for cancel-all).
- **Components**: CMP-192 OrderLineOverlay (context menu + Delete), CMP-230 OwnOrderMarker (cancel affordance in the "Your orders" column), CMP-043 Dialog / CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-229 ArmToggle, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge where relevant.
- Right-click (or Shift+F10 by keyboard) on an order line or ladder marker opens a context menu containing Cancel; `Delete` on a focused line/marker does the same, with a ConfirmDialog above the configurable notional threshold.
- Cancel single: `DELETE /api/v1/orders/{orderId}` via E31-T01, pending state until the `orders` WS event clears the line/marker.
- **Cancel-all on symbol**: the cancel-all key with the chart or ladder focused cancels all working orders on that symbol for the active target after the confirm policy, via `POST /api/v1/orders/cancel-all` with a symbol + account filter; results reported **per order**, with partial failures listed individually rather than a single blanket error.
- Already-filled translation: the exchange error for cancelling a filled order is translated to "Already filled" and the position view updates rather than showing a raw error.
- Disarmed/kill-switched/viewer states: cancel remains available where policy allows it (cancelling reduces risk) but must still respect RBAC and the kill-switch's documented semantics ("stops new risk, does not force-close") — the behaviour implemented is exactly what E31-D03/D06 specify, and the specified behaviour is restated in the UI.

## Out of scope
Flatten and cancel-all-across-symbols as a panic control (S06). Order blotter cancellation (E29 SCR-063). Trade-group cancel (E34's `/trade-groups/{id}/cancel`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Right-click cancel
  Given a working order line on the chart
  When I right-click it and choose Cancel
  Then the cancel is submitted and the line clears only when the orders WS event acknowledges it

Scenario: Cancel from the ladder marker
  Given my own order marker on a ladder row
  When I activate its cancel affordance
  Then the same cancel path runs and the marker clears on acknowledgement

Scenario: Cancel all on symbol
  Given three working orders on BTCUSDT for the active target
  When I press the cancel-all key with the chart focused
  Then the confirm policy applies and, on confirmation, all three are cancelled and reported individually

Scenario: Partial failure
  Given one of the three cancels fails
  Then the successful two are shown cancelled, the failure is listed with its reason, and no blanket success is claimed

Scenario: Already filled
  Given the order filled before the cancel arrived
  Then the exchange error is translated to "Already filled", the line clears, and the position view updates

Scenario: Keyboard cancel
  Given a keyboard user focuses an order line or a ladder marker
  When they press Delete
  Then the confirm applies above the notional threshold and the outcome is announced
```

## Technical notes / design
`POST /api/v1/orders/cancel-all` fans out `POST /v5/order/cancel-all` per account and Bybit costs 1 req/s per account for `linear`, so the fan-out scheduler serialises — the UI must therefore render a progressive per-order result list, not block on a single response.

Cancel round-trip budget ≤500 ms p95 (US-ORD-009 NFR).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: context-menu construction per line/marker kind; threshold logic for the confirm; error-code translation incl. the already-filled case; per-order result aggregation with mixed outcomes.
- **Integration**: cancel acknowledged, cancel-of-filled-order, cancel-all with one failing leg (recorded fixtures).
- **E2E**: place two orders on demo, cancel one from the chart and one from the ladder, then cancel-all with a third; assert exchange state matches.
- **A11y**: context menu reachable via Shift+F10, menu semantics, Delete path, announcements.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Order-cancelling path → `security`-labelled. Threats: a `viewer` cancelling another user's orders (RBAC re-checked server-side per account scope); mass-cancel as a denial-of-trading abuse (rate-limited, audited, confirmed); repudiation (every cancel audited with provenance and the surface used). Abuse case: attempt cancel-all against accounts outside the session's `account_scope` and assert 403 + no state change + audit row.

## Accessibility notes
Every mouse action has a keyboard twin (Shift+F10 menu, Delete key); the confirm dialog is an `alertdialog` with the action restated in the button's accessible name; per-order results are announced as a summary, not one live-region message per order.

## Performance notes
Cancel round trip ≤500 ms p95; the per-order result list renders progressively and must not block the frame.

## Observability
Audit `order.cancel_requested` with provenance (`source='chart-context'|'dom-marker'|'cancel-all-key'`); analytics `chart.cancel_from_chart`, `dom.cancel_from_ladder`; metric `cv_order_cancel_roundtrip_ms`.

title: Click-to-trade on the DOM ladder
body:
## Context
**US-DOM-007 — Click-to-trade from the DOM (Should):** *"As a trader, I want to place, modify and cancel orders directly on the ladder, so that execution matches my read."* E21 shipped SCR-050 with the trading affordances rendered **disabled**; this story turns them on. The ladder is the fastest execution surface in the product, so it has the tightest latency requirement (click→submit ≤50 ms client-side) and the strictest arm gating.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Screens**: SCR-050 (Heatmap + DOM ladder panel — the trading affordances), SCR-060 order ticket (the pre-filled hand-off when disarmed), SCR-076 (confirmation when policy requires), SCR-077 (rejection detail).
- **Components**: CMP-229 ArmToggle (scope `dom`, enabled for the first time), CMP-122 QuickSizeButtons (enabled — the active size preset resolves the click's quantity), CMP-230 OwnOrderMarker, CMP-108 DomLadderRow (trading variants), CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-232 LimitsChip, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog.
- Row interactions per the frozen modifier map (E31-D01/D06; the story baseline is: left-click a bid row = limit buy at that price, left-click an ask row = limit sell, Ctrl+click = market order, Escape = cancel all working orders on the symbol after the confirm policy).
- Quantity resolution: the active size preset from CMP-122 (per symbol-class and per account profile, US-ORD-003), with percent presets resolved to a concrete quantity and shown **before** submission.
- Hover preview on every row stating exactly what a click will do ("Limit buy 0.1 @ 64 100, account Main").
- Every placement carries the profile's native stop (server-enforced by E32; the UI shows CMP-158 so the guarantee is visible).
- **Disarmed path**: a click opens a pre-filled ticket requiring explicit confirmation instead of firing (US-DOM-007 scenario 3).
- Row target ≥24 px at every supported density; the arm state and environment badge are always visible on the panel, and no trading affordance is operable unless both are.
- Guard integration with E31-T01 for kill-switch, lockouts, RBAC (`viewer` sees the ladder read-only), stale/disconnected book (trading affordances hard-disabled when the book is stale or resynchronising — you may not trade against a frozen book).
- **Keyboard**: the ladder's roving-tabindex grid gains a row action menu on Enter containing every mouse action (place limit, place market, cancel my order, move my order), with the confirm policy applied identically.

## Out of scope
Ladder rendering, heatmap, depth tiers, colour scale, own-order data plumbing (all E21). Drag-to-modify (S05). Cancel-all as a global panic action (S06). Sizing rule definitions (E28/E30).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Limit placement
  Given one-click trading is armed on the ladder and the active preset is 0.1 BTC
  When I left-click a bid row at 64 100
  Then a limit buy of 0.1 at 64 100 is submitted with a native stop attached per the profile,
  the own-order marker appears in pending state, and the acknowledgement arrives within 500 ms

Scenario: Market order
  When I Ctrl+click a row
  Then a market order for the active size is submitted after the configured confirm policy

Scenario: Cancel all on symbol
  When I press Escape with the ladder focused
  Then all working orders on that symbol for the active target are cancelled after the confirm policy

Scenario: Disarmed
  Given one-click trading is locked
  When I click a row
  Then a pre-filled ticket opens requiring explicit confirmation and nothing is submitted

Scenario: Stale or resynchronising book
  Given the book is stale or resynchronising
  Then row trading affordances are disabled with a stated reason and no click can submit

Scenario: Read-only role
  Given the session role is viewer
  Then the ladder renders read-only, no trading affordance is operable,
  and a forced request is rejected server-side with 403, no state change and an audit row

Scenario: Latency
  Given an armed ladder under a live 200-depth book
  Then click to submit completes within 50 ms client-side at p95

Scenario: Keyboard placement
  Given a keyboard user on a focused ladder row
  When they press Enter and choose "Place limit buy"
  Then the same intent is produced, the confirm policy applies, and the outcome is announced
```

## Technical notes / design
The click handler must read from already-decoded book state (the shared worker) and the cached instrument filters — no fetch is permitted on the interaction path, or the 50 ms budget is unreachable.

Quantity from a percent preset is resolved from the cached `wallet` WS state; if that state is stale, percent presets are disabled with the reason stated (mirroring US-ORD-014's stale-input rule) rather than resolving from stale equity.

All submissions go through `packages/trading-intent` (E31-T01); duplicate suppression there protects against double-fire on a noisy pointer.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: row→intent mapping for each modifier and each side; preset resolution incl. percent and invalid-for-symbol presets; stale-book and stale-wallet disabling; hover-preview text; the disarmed hand-off payload.
- **Component**: CMP-108 trading variants and CMP-230 markers in Storybook (armed, locked, pending, rejected, viewer-read-only); axe on each.
- **Integration**: submit→ack via the `orders` topic; rejection fixtures (post-only, reduce-only violation, `10018`).
- **E2E (web + Electron)**: arm, click a bid row on demo, assert the order exists on the exchange with the expected price and a native stop; attempt while disarmed and assert a ticket opened with zero submissions.
- **Perf**: click→submit p95 ≤50 ms under a live 200-depth book with the heatmap active; verify the ladder still meets its own E21 render budget with markers enabled.
- **A11y**: axe-core on SCR-050 with trading on; keyboard placement through the row action menu; target size at compact density; announcement assertions.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Highest-risk surface in the epic: one click = one live order. Threats — accidental fire (arm gate, hover preview, confirm policy, ≥24 px targets, undo window), wrong-account fire (the active target is displayed persistently with the arm indicator per US-ORD-005), privilege escalation (`viewer` read-only, server re-check on `account_scope`), rate-limit abuse (duplicate suppression + governor awareness), repudiation (every click-trade audited with the price row and modifier used — the explicit US-DOM-007 NFR). Manual abuse cases required: fire while disarmed, while kill-switched, while locked out, as a `viewer`, and against an out-of-scope account. Data classification: financial, audited.

## Accessibility notes
The ladder is a `role="grid"` with roving tabindex (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §4.2); every mouse action exists in the Enter-activated row action menu; own-order markers are text in a dedicated "Your orders" column so nothing depends on a canvas glyph (CMP-230); arm state changes announce assertively; pending/acknowledged/rejected announce per the E31-D05 script.

## Performance notes
Budgets: click→submit ≤50 ms client-side; click→ack p95 <300 ms demo (budget #4); the ladder's own render budget from E21 must not regress with markers and trading affordances enabled.

## Observability
Audit `order.submitted` with `source='dom-click'`, `price_row`, `modifier`; analytics `dom.click_trade`, `dom.arm_toggled`; metrics `cv_chart_trade_click_to_submit_ms{source="dom-click"}`, `cv_trading_intent_refused_total{reason}`.

title: Drag an order marker on the ladder to reprice it
body:
## Context
**US-DOM-008 — Drag to modify from the DOM (Should):** *"As a trader, I want to drag my order marker to another price, so that I reprice without retyping."* This is the ladder twin of E31-S02 and reuses its pending/spring-back/undo machinery; the difference is that the drop target is a discrete ladder **row**, not a continuous price, which removes the snapping ambiguity but adds row-boundary edge cases.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Screens**: SCR-050 (marker drag), SCR-077 (rejection detail).
- **Components**: CMP-230 OwnOrderMarker (grab, drag, drop-valid, drop-invalid, pending, return-to-origin), CMP-108 DomLadderRow (drop-target states), CMP-044 ConfirmDialog for above-threshold moves.
- Drag lifecycle: grab a marker → rows highlight as valid/invalid drop targets → drop on a row → `PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}` at that row's price via E31-T01 → marker shows **pending** → clears on the `orders` WS event, or **returns to its original row** with the exact reason on rejection.
- Aggregate markers: when several of my orders rest at one price (or a group aggregate marker is shown), dragging must either disambiguate explicitly or move the whole set as specified in E31-D03 — never silently pick one.
- Refusals before sending: dragging a reduce-only stop to the wrong side of the market is refused inline and nothing is sent (US-DOM-008 scenario 3).
- **Reconciliation guarantee**: the optimistic marker position must reconcile with exchange truth within 1 s or be marked unreconciled (US-DOM-008 NFR) — never left looking settled.
- Undo window applies identically to chart drags (E31-T01).
- **Keyboard equivalent**: row action menu → "Move my order" → arrow keys move the target row → Enter commits → Esc abandons; announced per the E31-D05 script.
- Auto-scroll behaviour when dragging toward the edge of the visible ladder window, with the auto-centring suppressed during a drag so the target row cannot move under the pointer.

## Out of scope
Placement (S04), cancellation (S03), chart drags (S02), ladder rendering and auto-centring policy (E21).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Drag reprice
  Given my working limit order marker on a ladder row
  When I drag it to another row and release
  Then an amend to that row's price is submitted and the marker shows pending until acknowledged

Scenario: Amend rejected
  Given the exchange rejects the amend
  Then the marker returns to its original price and the exact reason is shown

Scenario: Drag onto invalid price
  When I drag a reduce-only stop to the wrong side of the market
  Then the drop is refused with an inline explanation and nothing is sent

Scenario: Optimistic state always reconciles
  Given an amend was acknowledged by REST but no orders WS event arrives within one second
  Then the marker is shown as unreconciled rather than settled, and the reconciliation loop resolves it

Scenario: Ladder must not move under the pointer
  Given auto-centring is enabled and price moves during a drag
  Then recentring is suppressed for the duration of the drag and resumes on release

Scenario: Multiple orders at one price
  Given two of my orders rest at the same price
  When I begin a drag on that marker
  Then the UI disambiguates explicitly and never silently repositions the wrong order

Scenario: Keyboard move
  Given a keyboard user on their own order's row
  When they choose "Move my order", press arrow keys and Enter
  Then the amend is submitted to the selected row's price and the outcome is announced
```

## Technical notes / design
Drop target is the row's price, already tick-aligned by the ladder's aggregation; when the ladder is aggregating multiple ticks per row (E21 tick aggregation), the amend price must be the row's canonical price and that must be stated in the hover/preview text so the user is not surprised.

Amend semantics, error codes and the pending/spring-back machinery are shared with E31-S02 — this story must **reuse** `packages/trading-intent` rather than re-implementing, and a reviewer should reject any duplicated guard logic.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: row→price resolution incl. the tick-aggregated case; wrong-side detection; aggregate-marker disambiguation; auto-scroll and recentre suppression; keyboard move arithmetic.
- **Component**: CMP-230 stories for every drag state; axe.
- **Integration**: amend ack / reject / late-ack (unreconciled) with recorded fixtures.
- **E2E**: place an order on demo from the ladder, drag it two rows, assert the exchange price matches the target row; drag a stop to the wrong side and assert zero network calls.
- **Perf**: drag does not regress the ladder's E21 render budget; reconciliation within 1 s asserted in the integration test.
- **A11y**: keyboard move path; announcements at commit and resolve only.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Order-modifying path → `security`-labelled. Threats: wrong-order repricing via ambiguous aggregate markers (explicit disambiguation is the control), optimistic display of a state the exchange never accepted (the 1 s reconciliation rule is the control), repudiation (audit with `source='dom-drag'`, old and new price, and the row). Abuse case: attempt to amend an order belonging to an account outside `account_scope` and assert 403 + no state change + audit.

## Accessibility notes
Drag is never the only path; the row action menu carries the move operation. Recentre suppression during keyboard move as well as pointer drag, so an AT user's target does not shift mid-operation. Announcements throttled to commit/resolve.

## Performance notes
Amend round trip ≤500 ms p95; reconciliation deadline 1 s; the ladder must keep its E21 frame budget while a drag is in progress.

## Observability
Audit `order.amend_requested` with `source='dom-drag'`, `price_row`, old/new price; analytics `dom.drag_amend`; metric `cv_trading_unreconciled_total`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated; coverage met; no duplicated guard logic (reviewer-checked).
- [ ] axe-core green; keyboard path verified; SR pass.
- [ ] Security review; abuse case executed.
- [ ] Design QA; QA sign-off; demoed.

title: One-click flatten, cancel-all and reverse with the confirmation policy
body:
## Context
**US-ORD-010 — Flatten and cancel-all (Must)** and **US-ORD-011 — Reverse position (Should)**. These are the exit controls: the ones a trader reaches for when something is going wrong, and therefore the ones that must be fastest, most reliable and least ambiguous. They are also the most destructive, so the confirm policy and the per-account result reporting matter as much as the action itself.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Screens**: SCR-063 Positions & orders grid (the flatten entry point per the traceability matrix), SCR-072 Kill-switch / freeze confirmation modal (the flatten / cancel-all confirmation variant), SCR-076 Order confirmation modal (the **reverse** variant), SCR-030 and SCR-050 (the chart/ladder entry points and the flatten/reverse hotkeys in those scopes).
- **Components**: CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-027 ErrorState/InlineError, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-093, CMP-123, CMP-211 (per the SCR-072 catalogue entry), CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-130 SlippageEstimateChip, CMP-232 LimitsChip, CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal (per SCR-076).
- **Flatten symbol**: cancel working orders then close the position with a **reduce-only market order** (never a plain market order — reversal by accident is the failure mode being designed out), reported as **one operation** with a per-step result. Uses `POST /api/v1/orders/cancel-all` + `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/close`.
- **Flatten group**: each account flattens; results reported **per account**; a failed leg is retried **once** automatically and the residual failure is surfaced with a next action (US-ORD-010 scenario 2). Completes within 2 s for 5 accounts.
- **Nothing to flatten**: reports "nothing to flatten" with **no exchange call at all** (asserted by a network-level test).
- **Reverse**: `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/reverse` — closes and opens the opposite side in one operation with a fresh native stop attached in the same operation (US-ORD-011 NFR: never leave a position without a stop after a reverse). Reverse **always requires explicit confirmation even when one-click is armed**, and the confirmation restates current position, resulting position, quantity, the stop that will attach, and margin required vs available.
- **Insufficient margin**: refused *before* sending, showing required versus available margin.
- Confirm policy integration: immediate / hold-to-confirm / dialog per environment, with LIVE never permitted to skip; destructive hotkeys default to hold-to-confirm (US-ORD-006 NFR).
- Kill-switch interaction documented and implemented per its stated semantics ("stops new risk, does not force-close") — flatten is a separate, documented panic path (`POST /api/v1/positions/close-all` is the flatten-all control referenced by SCR-072) and the UI must make the distinction explicit rather than implying the kill-switch closes positions.

## Out of scope
The kill-switch control itself and risk lockouts (E39). Trade-group definition and fan-out scheduling/rate governance (E28/E34) — this story consumes the group target and reports per-leg outcomes. Blotter-level bulk actions beyond flatten (E29).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Flatten symbol
  Given an open BTCUSDT position and two working orders on account A
  When I flatten BTCUSDT on account A
  Then the working orders are cancelled and the position is closed with a reduce-only market order,
  and the whole thing is reported to me as one operation with its per-step results

Scenario: Flatten group
  Given a trade group of three accounts, one of which fails on the first attempt
  Then each account's result is reported separately, the failed leg is retried once automatically,
  and a residual failure is shown with an explicit next action

Scenario: Flatten with nothing open
  Given no position and no working orders
  Then the action reports "nothing to flatten" and makes no exchange call

Scenario: Reverse
  Given a long of 0.2 BTC
  When I confirm a reverse
  Then a market order of 0.4 is sent, the resulting short is shown, and a fresh native stop is attached in the same operation

Scenario: Reverse always confirms
  Given one-click trading is armed
  When I trigger reverse
  Then explicit confirmation is still required and the LIVE variant offers no "don't ask again"

Scenario: Insufficient margin
  Given margin is insufficient for the resulting position
  Then the reverse is refused before any exchange call, showing required versus available margin

Scenario: Destructive hotkey is not a single tap
  Given the flatten hotkey with the default policy
  Then it requires hold-to-confirm, and a single tap does nothing

Scenario: Timing
  Given a flatten across five accounts
  Then the operation completes within two seconds
```

## Technical notes / design
Flatten is composed, not atomic at the exchange: cancel-all then reduce-only close. The UI must therefore model it as a small local saga with per-step state, and must never report success until both steps have their acknowledgements — a cancelled-but-not-closed outcome is a visible partial state, not a success.

Reduce-only is mandatory on the close leg (US-ORD-010 NFR). `POST /api/v1/positions/close-all` is the flatten-all panic control referenced from SCR-072; the symbol/account-scoped flatten uses the per-position endpoint.

Automatic retry is exactly **one** attempt, with jitter, and must respect the rate-limit governor; a second failure escalates to the user rather than looping.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: saga state machine (cancel ok/close fail, cancel fail/close ok, both fail, nothing-open short-circuit); per-account result aggregation; single-retry logic; margin pre-check arithmetic; confirm-policy resolution per environment and per action.
- **Integration**: recorded fixtures for a failing close, a `10018` rate-limited leg, and an exchange 5xx mid-flatten.
- **E2E (web + Electron)**: on demo, open a position, flatten it from SCR-063 and assert both cancellation and closure on the exchange; reverse a position and assert the resulting side, size and the attached stop; trigger flatten with nothing open and assert **zero** network calls.
- **Chaos** (feeds E31-Q04): kill the WS mid-flatten and assert the operation reconciles to a correct, visible state.
- **Perf**: 5-account flatten within 2 s.
- **A11y**: confirmation dialogs as `alertdialog`, focus trap and return, action restated in the accessible name, per-account results announced as a summary.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend; the saga module held to ≥90 % as a risk module.

## Security notes
Destructive, position-closing path → `security`-labelled. Threats: accidental flatten/reverse (hold-to-confirm, always-confirm on reverse, no default-focused confirm for LIVE market actions per SCR-076), unauthorised flatten of another user's accounts (server-side `account_scope` re-check), accidental **reversal** instead of close (reduce-only on the close leg is the structural control), and leaving a position unprotected after a reverse (stop attaches in the same operation; E32 enforces server-side). Repudiation: every flatten/reverse audited per account with the operation id. Abuse cases: flatten accounts outside scope; reverse while kill-switched; reverse with the SL attachment stubbed to fail, asserting the documented failure policy fires.

## Accessibility notes
Hold-to-confirm must have a keyboard-operable equivalent that is not a timed key-hold trap for AT users (per E31-D05: a dialog path is always available); the confirm button's accessible name restates the whole action; `Enter` confirms only after the 400 ms guard (SCR-076); per-account results are a table, not a stream of alerts.

## Performance notes
Flatten across 5 accounts ≤2 s; hotkey→submit ≤50 ms client-side; the confirmation modal is prepared from loaded state and appears ≤100 ms (SCR-076).

## Observability
Audit `position.flattened`, `position.reversed`, `order.cancel_requested` (per account, with the operation id and provenance); analytics `trading.flatten_invoked`, `trading.reverse_invoked`, `order.confirmation_shown/cancelled`; metrics `cv_flatten_duration_ms{accounts}`, `cv_flatten_leg_failures_total`.

title: Chart/DOM trading intent layer: guards, optimistic state, undo window and audit
body:
## Context
S01–S06 are six different surfaces that all produce the same three things: an **order intent**, a **guard decision**, and an **optimistic pending state that must reconcile with exchange truth**. Implementing that logic six times guarantees six different bugs and six different ways to bypass a safety gate. This Task builds it once, as a frontend package module consumed by every E31 story, plus the thin backend enrichment needed to audit the *manner* of the action.

The client is never the authority: the OMS (E29) and the native-SL invariant (E32/M17) validate server-side regardless of what this layer decides (US-ORD-005 NFR). This layer exists to refuse early, to render honestly, and to make every action auditable.

## Scope / Deliverables
**Frontend — `packages/trading-intent` (new module inside the web app):**
- `TradeIntent` type: `{ source: 'chart-click'|'chart-drag'|'dom-click'|'dom-drag'|'flatten'|'reverse'|'cancel', symbol, side, orderType, price?, triggerPrice?, triggerBy?, qty, reduceOnly, accountIds[] | tradeGroupId, modifier, priceRow?, correlationId }`.
- **Guard chain**, evaluated in a fixed order with the first failure returned as a structured reason: kill-switch engaged (from `auth_ok.kill_switch` and the `system` WS topic) → risk lockout active (E39) → RBAC (`orders:write` / `positions:write` on the target accounts, from the session permission set) → environment/arm state (CMP-229 scope `chart`/`dom`, US-ORD-005; auto-disarm on 30 min inactivity, session lock, environment switch or disconnect) → instrument filters (`priceFilter` tick snapping and `lotSizeFilter` min/step from `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}`) → side/price sanity (a stop on the wrong side of the mark, a limit on the wrong side for the chosen type — US-ORD-007 scenario 3, US-ORD-008 scenario 3) → confirm policy resolution (immediate / hold-to-confirm / dialog, per environment; LIVE may never skip).
- **Snap-to-tick** helper: round-half-away-from-zero to `tickSize`, returning both the snapped price and a flag so the UI can show "Snapped to 0.5 tick".
- **Submission adapter**: maps intent → `POST /api/v1/orders`, `PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `DELETE /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `POST /api/v1/orders/cancel-all`, `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/close`, `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/reverse`, `PUT /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/tpsl`. Every request carries a client-generated `orderLinkId`-derived idempotency key (ADR-0006) so a double-fire from a jittery pointer cannot double-submit.
- **Pending/reconcile store**: an intent enters `pending` on send; it clears only when the matching `orders`/`positions` WS event arrives (WS is the source of truth — REST ack is acceptance only, ADR-0006). If no reconciling event arrives within **1 s** (US-DOM-008 NFR), the UI shows an unreconciled warning; the optimistic visual **springs back** on a rejection with the exact exchange reason, routed to SCR-077 for detail.
- **Undo window**: configurable (default from the E31-D01 research figure), during which a submitted-not-yet-filled intent can be reverted — cancel for a placement, re-amend to the original price for a drag. If the order already filled, the undo control changes to state that plainly and offers the flatten path instead; it never silently market-closes. Every undo emits its own audited action.
- Error-code → copy mapping from the E31-D06 copy deck, covering `order_not_amendable`, validation failures, already-filled cancels, insufficient margin and `10018` rate limiting.

**Backend — module M14 (OMS) enrichment only:**
- Accept and persist the interaction provenance on order submission: `source`, `modifier`, `price_row` in the `orders` request payload, written to `order_events` (`event_type='local_create'`, payload) and to `audit_log`, so US-DOM-007's NFR ("every click-trade action audited with the price row and modifier used") is satisfiable.
- Reject unknown `source` values; `source` is advisory metadata and must never influence validation or ordering.

## Out of scope
Any UI (S01–S06). The OMS state machine, reconciliation loop and blotters (E29). Native-SL attachment logic (E32) — this layer only *refuses to construct* an entry intent without an SL when the profile requires it, and lets the server be the enforcer. Fan-out scheduling (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Guards run in order and refuse early
  Given the kill-switch is engaged and one-click is also disarmed
  When any surface builds an intent
  Then the guard chain returns the kill-switch reason (the highest-precedence failure), nothing is sent,
  and the refusal is logged with the intent's correlation id

Scenario: Double-fire cannot double-submit
  Given a pointer emits two pointerdown events 8 ms apart on the same ladder row
  Then exactly one request is sent, carrying one idempotency key, and the second is dropped as a duplicate

Scenario: Price is snapped before anything is sent
  Given tickSize 0.5 and a pointer price of 64 100.37
  Then the intent carries 64 100.5 and a snapped flag the UI can surface

Scenario: Optimistic state reconciles or springs back
  Given an amend is submitted and the exchange rejects it
  Then the pending state clears, the visual returns to the pre-drag value,
  and the exact exchange message and code are available to the caller

Scenario: Unreconciled after one second
  Given a REST ack was received but no orders WS event arrived within 1000 ms
  Then the intent is marked unreconciled and the caller is told, rather than being shown a confirmed state

Scenario: Undo after fill is honest
  Given an undo is attempted on an order that already filled
  Then no reversing market order is sent automatically; the caller is told it filled and offered the flatten path

Scenario: Provenance is audited
  Given a DOM click-trade at price row 64 100 with the Ctrl modifier
  Then the persisted order_events row and audit_log entry both record source='dom-click', modifier='ctrl', price_row=64100
```

## Technical notes / design
Guard chain is a pure function `evaluate(intent, context) -> Ok(intent') | Refused(reason)` so it is exhaustively unit-testable without a DOM. Context is assembled from the session (`auth_ok` permissions, `allowed_environments`, `kill_switch`), the arm store, the risk-cap store and the instrument cache.

Idempotency: `orderLinkId = <sessionId>-<monotonicSeq>-<hash(intent)>`, matching the uniqueness constraint `ux_orders_link` on `orders`.

Pending store keys on the idempotency key, not on the exchange order id, because the exchange id is not known until acceptance.

Config keys: `trading.undo_window_ms`, `trading.arm_timeout_seconds` (already in the settings payload), `trading.confirm_market_orders`, `trading.confirm_flatten`, `trading.reconcile_timeout_ms` (default 1000).

## Test plan
- **Unit** (target ≥90 % on this module, it is a risk module): each guard in isolation and in precedence order; snap-to-tick at boundaries (exact tick, half tick, negative drift, very small tick sizes); idempotency key generation and duplicate suppression; pending→acknowledged, pending→rejected, pending→unreconciled transitions; undo before ack, after ack, after fill; error-code→copy mapping exhaustive over the documented codes.
- **Contract**: request bodies validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml` schemas for every endpoint used; provenance fields validated against the OpenAPI order-create schema.
- **Integration** (backend): submitting with provenance writes the expected `order_events` and `audit_log` rows; unknown `source` rejected.
- **Fixtures**: recorded Bybit rejection fixtures (post-only reject, reduce-only violation, `10018`), plus a WS fixture that acks late (1.5 s) to exercise the unreconciled path.

## Security notes
Threats (`04-security-program.md`, STRIDE from E31-X01): **Tampering** — a client that forges `source` to look benign is possible, hence provenance is advisory-only and never affects validation. **Elevation of privilege** — the guard chain must not be the only RBAC check; the server re-checks account scope on every call. **Repudiation** — provenance + correlation id close the "I never clicked that" gap. **Denial of service** — duplicate suppression and the client-side rate awareness prevent a pointer storm from burning the per-UID rate budget. Data classification: financial, audited. Requires the `security` label and Security engineer review.

## Accessibility notes
The module is headless but must expose the state transitions (pending/acknowledged/rejected/unreconciled) as first-class values so consuming UIs can announce them per the E31-D05 utterance script; it must also throttle change notifications during a drag to commit/resolve moments only, to avoid live-region storms.

## Performance notes
Guard evaluation plus snapping must complete in ≤5 ms so the end-to-end click→submit budget of 50 ms (US-DOM-007 NFR) is dominated by transport, not logic. Emits `cv_chart_trade_click_to_submit_ms`. The instrument filter data must be read from cache, never fetched on the interaction path.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_chart_trade_click_to_submit_ms` (histogram, labelled by source), `cv_trading_intent_refused_total{reason}`, `cv_trading_unreconciled_total`, `cv_trading_undo_total{outcome}`. Audit: provenance on `order.submitted`, `order.amend_requested`, `order.cancel_requested`, plus a new `trading.undo_used`. Logs carry the correlation id end to end.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Module shipped with ≥90 % unit coverage; backend enrichment ≥85 %.
- [ ] OpenAPI updated for the provenance fields; contract tests green.
- [ ] Docs: `24-internal-schemas.md` notes the provenance fields on the order create path.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment; SAST/SCA clean.
- [ ] Metrics visible in Grafana; audit rows verified on demo.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E31-K01** (proven latency/hit-testing approach, Sprint 16), **E29** (OMS, order state machine and the private `orders`/`positions`/`executions` WS mirror — completes **S16**), **E39** (risk caps, lockouts and the kill-switch whose state this layer must read before every intent — completes **S16**), and **E31-D03** (handoff package incl. the error-code→copy deck, Done end of S15).

**Scheduling.** Every blocker of this ticket completes no later than **Sprint 16**, so the Sprint-17 start is strictly after its dependencies rather than concurrent with them.

**E30 / E32 are consumed, not blocking, here.** E30 (order ticket, arm/lock, confirm policy) and E32 (brackets + native-SL invariant) run S16–S17 and complete at the end of S17. This ticket integrates against their **interfaces frozen at the end of S16** — the `ArmState` contract, the confirmation-policy config key and the server-side native-SL rejection code — published as part of those epics' S16 output. The E31 tickets that need E30/E32 *behaviour* rather than their interface (E31-S02, S03, S05, S06) are scheduled in **Sprint 18**, strictly after E30 and E32 close in S17. That split is the slack mechanism keeping this epic inside the S17–S18 window.

title: STRIDE threat model for chart and DOM trading interactions
body:
## Context
`04-security-program.md` mandates a STRIDE threat model per epic, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 makes it default-on for any epic touching the OMS. E31 adds four new order-originating paths (chart click, chart drag, DOM click, DOM drag) plus two destructive ones (flatten, reverse). Each is a new place where an order can be created, so each is a new place where the safety architecture can be bypassed. The model must be done in Sprint 16 so its controls are inputs to E31-T01, not retrofits.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model over the E31 data flow: pointer/keyboard event → intent construction → client guard chain → REST call → OMS validation → exchange → private WS → optimistic-state reconciliation → audit.
- Enumerate and rate (likelihood × impact) at minimum:
  - **Spoofing**: a forged `source`/`modifier` provenance field; a replayed request with a reused idempotency key.
  - **Tampering**: client-side manipulation of the arm state or the guard chain to reach a submission path; manipulation of the cached instrument filters to defeat tick/lot validation; DOM-mirror manipulation to move a line the user cannot see.
  - **Repudiation**: "I never clicked that" — coverage of the audit trail for every surface, incl. undo actions and keyboard paths.
  - **Information disclosure**: ghost lines or aggregate markers exposing accounts outside the session's `account_scope`; rejection details leaking exchange credentials or internal identifiers.
  - **Denial of service**: pointer-storm order flooding burning the per-UID rate budget and denying the user the ability to exit a position (the most dangerous DoS in this product); mass cancel-all abuse.
  - **Elevation of privilege**: a `viewer` reaching an order-placing path through a keyboard shortcut, a context menu or a direct API call.
- For each threat: existing control, gap, and the required mitigation with an owning ticket (mitigations land in E31-T01 or the relevant story; anything not mitigated is an explicit accepted risk with Owner sign-off).
- Explicit treatment of the **safety invariant**: enumerate every way an E31 path could produce a position without a native exchange-side stop, and confirm each is closed server-side (client-side refusals are convenience only).
- Abuse-case list handed to E31-X02 and to E31-Q01 so the negative cases are tested, not just modelled.
- Data-classification statement for everything E31 touches (financial, audited; no PII beyond the acting user id).

## Out of scope
The OMS state machine's own threat model (E29-X), key vault (E27), fan-out (E34) — reference them rather than re-deriving.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every STRIDE category covered for every new path
  Given four order-originating and two destructive paths
  Then each has at least one enumerated threat per applicable STRIDE category, with likelihood, impact and a control

Scenario: Invariant escape analysis is exhaustive
  Then every hypothesised route to an unprotected position is listed with the server-side control that closes it,
  and any route without one becomes a P0 ticket

Scenario: Mitigations have owners
  Then every identified gap maps to a specific ticket key, or to a recorded accepted risk signed by the Owner
```

## Technical notes / design
Model against the actual endpoints (`/orders`, `/orders/{id}` PATCH/DELETE, `/orders/cancel-all`, `/positions/{id}/close|reverse|tpsl`, `/positions/close-all`) and the private WS topics, using the architecture module M14 boundary as the trust boundary — everything client-side is untrusted.

## Test plan
The model's assertions become test cases: each claimed control must name the test (unit, E2E safety sweep, or manual abuse case) that proves it.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security analysis; output is reviewed by the Security engineer and the Architect, and its Critical/High findings must be closed before the R3 Security gate.

## Accessibility notes
Include the a11y paths in the model explicitly — keyboard shortcuts and AT-driven interactions are order-placing paths and must not be modelled as second-class.

## Performance notes
The DoS analysis must consider the rate-limit budget interaction: client-side duplicate suppression and back-off are security controls here, not just UX.

## Observability
Specify the security-relevant telemetry: refusal counts by reason, anomalous submission-rate detection, and the audit fields that make repudiation impossible.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Model documented in the security space and linked from E31.
- [ ] All threats rated; all Critical/High have mitigations with ticket keys or signed accepted risk.
- [ ] Invariant escape analysis complete with server-side controls named.
- [ ] Abuse-case list handed to E31-X02 and E31-Q01.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed by the Security engineer and the Architect.

title: Abuse cases, RBAC/arm bypass checks and security sign-off for trading surfaces
body:
## Context
E31-X01 produces the theory; this ticket produces the proof and the automation. Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2, anything touching order placement requires a *manual abuse-case check* — attempting the attack, not just reasoning about it — plus clean SAST/SCA.

The final security gate for E31 before the epic can be Done and before R3's Security quality gate is assessed. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 states that anything touching order placement is treated as `security`-labelled for DoD purposes whether or not the label was applied — this ticket is where that is enforced across all E31 children.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Executed abuse cases** against demo, each with recorded evidence (request, response, UI state, audit row):
  1. Place an order from chart and from ladder while **disarmed** — expect refusal, no request, logged.
  2. Same while the **kill-switch is engaged** — expect refusal at the client and rejection (`trading_disabled`) at the server if forced.
  3. Same while a **risk lockout** is active (E39) — expect refusal + audit.
  4. As a **`viewer`** role: exercise every E31 affordance in the UI (expect hard-disabled) and force each endpoint directly (expect 403, **no state change**, audit row).
  5. Against an **account outside `account_scope`**: force order create, amend, cancel, close and reverse — expect 403 + audit for each.
  6. **Idempotency replay**: resend an identical order request with the same key — expect exactly one order.
  7. **Provenance forgery**: submit with a fabricated `source`/`modifier`/`price_row` — expect the order to be validated identically (provenance advisory only) and the forged value recorded as-received without influencing behaviour; confirm unknown `source` values are rejected.
  8. **Filter tampering**: submit a price off-tick and a quantity off-lot directly to the API — expect server-side rejection regardless of client-side snapping.
  9. **Invariant bypass attempt**: attempt, via each E31 path and via direct API calls, to open a position without a native stop — expect zero escapes (this is R3 exit criterion 2 and must be evidenced here as well as in the E2E sweep).
  10. **Order flood**: burst submissions from the ladder path — expect duplicate suppression, governor back-off, and — critically — that the user can still **exit** a position while throttled (exit paths must not be starved by entry flooding).
- **SAST/Semgrep rules** added for this area: flag any component issuing an order/position mutation without going through `packages/trading-intent`; flag any client-side-only authorisation check presented as the sole gate; flag direct `fetch` to order endpoints outside the adapter.
- **DAST**: ZAP profile additions covering the E31 endpoints with an authenticated `viewer` session, asserting 403 on every mutation.
- SCA/secrets scan confirmation for the new frontend module.

- **White-box review** of the shipped code for: `packages/trading-intent` (guard chain ordering, idempotency, reconciliation), the chart trading layer, the ladder trading affordances, the flatten/reverse saga, and the M14 provenance enrichment.
- Verify against the E31-X01 model that every claimed control exists in code and is covered by a named test; any control that is asserted but untested is a finding.
- Confirm: client-side checks are never the sole gate; the server validates independently on every path; provenance cannot influence validation; RBAC is enforced per account on every mutation; the safety invariant has no E31-reachable escape.
- Review the audit completeness: every E31 action type produces an audit row with actor, account, symbol, surface, modifier, price and correlation id, and the `audit_log` hash chain still verifies after an E31-heavy session.
- Confirm the R3 Security gate items relevant to E31: STRIDE findings all Critical/High closed; abuse-case results recorded; SAST/DAST/SCA clean or triaged.
- Post the sign-off comment on E31 and on each child story that requires one; record any accepted risks with Owner sign-off and an expiry/review date.
- Hand the residual risk list to E43 (hardening & pen-test remediation) so the pre-R4 pen-test scopes these surfaces explicitly.

## Out of scope
Pen-test (E43, pre-R4). Key vault abuse cases (E27). Fan-out partial-failure abuse (E34).

Re-running the abuse cases (E31-X02) or the QA pass (E31-Q06) — this ticket consumes their evidence.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every abuse case executed with evidence
  Given the ten cases
  Then each has a recorded attempt, the observed result, and the audit row it produced

Scenario: No escape from the safety invariant
  Given every E31 path and direct API calls
  Then no attempt produces a position without a native exchange-side stop

Scenario: Exit is never starved
  Given an order flood that trips the rate governor
  Then flatten and cancel remain possible for the user within the documented time, and this is demonstrated

Scenario: SAST rules catch a real violation
  Given a deliberately introduced direct fetch to the order endpoint from a component
  Then the Semgrep rule fails the build
```

Direct-API attempts use the same session tokens the UI would hold, to prove server-side enforcement rather than client-side absence. Every forced attempt must be verified to produce an audit row — a silent 403 is itself a finding.

Review with the E31-X01 model open as the checklist; treat the guard-chain ordering as the highest-value review target, since a reordering bug silently weakens every surface at once.
